ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels.type:
(n k : Nat) → 1 ≤ n →
  Set (Set (Fin k → Nat)) × Set (Set (Fin k → Nat)) × Set (Set (Fin k → Nat))
ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels.value:
fun n k _ =>
  let quantify : (m : Nat) → Bool → ((Fin m → Nat) → Prop) → Prop :=
    Nat.rec (motive := fun m => Bool → ((Fin m → Nat) → Prop) → Prop)
      (fun _ matrix => matrix Fin.elim0)
      (fun _ ih existential matrix =>
        if existential then
          ∃ y : Nat, ih false (fun ys => matrix (Fin.cons y ys))
        else
          ∀ y : Nat, ih true (fun ys => matrix (Fin.cons y ys)))
  let sigma : Set (Set (Fin k → Nat)) :=
    {A | ∃ R : (Fin k → Nat) → (Fin n → Nat) → Prop,
      PrimrecRel R ∧ ∀ xs : Fin k → Nat, xs ∈ A ↔ quantify n true (R xs)}
  let pi : Set (Set (Fin k → Nat)) := {A | Aᶜ ∈ sigma}
  (sigma, pi, sigma ∩ pi)
ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels.sourceReason: The general definition is supplied only by the Alphabeta Math Shared Math Library item def-sigma-n-pi-n-and-delta-n-sets (https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-sigma-n-pi-n-and-delta-n-sets). The article-specific Research Portal and the supplied defect report (https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects) both returned HTTP 404. PrimrecRel represents the primitive-recursive matrix, including the permitted bounded quantifiers.

RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability.type: Set Nat → (Set Nat → Prop) × (Set Nat → Prop) × ((Nat → Nat) → Prop)
RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability.value:
fun X =>
  let Program (states symbols : Nat) :=
    Fin (states + 3) →
      Sum (Fin (symbols + 4) → Fin (states + 3) × Fin (symbols + 4) × Bool)
        (Fin (states + 3) × Fin (states + 3))
  let Configuration (states symbols : Nat) :=
    Fin (states + 3) × Nat × List (Fin (symbols + 4))
  let numeral (symbols n : Nat) : List (Fin (symbols + 4)) :=
    List.map (fun digit => if digit = '0' then 0 else 1) (Nat.toDigits 2 n)
  let readNumeral (symbols : Nat) (tape : List (Fin (symbols + 4))) (start : Nat) :
      Option Nat :=
    let tail := List.drop start tape
    let word := List.takeWhile (fun digit => digit != 3) tail
    let n := List.foldl (fun acc digit => 2 * acc + Fin.val digit) 0 word
    if List.getD tail (List.length word) 2 = 3 ∧ word = numeral symbols n then
      Option.some n
    else
      Option.none
  let halting (states : Nat) (state : Fin (states + 3)) : Bool :=
    state == 1 || state == 2
  let step (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols)
      (config nextConfig : Configuration states symbols) : Prop :=
    let (state, head, tape) := config
    halting states state = false ∧
      match program state with
      | Sum.inl ordinary =>
        let (next, symbol, right) := ordinary (List.getD tape head 2)
        let padded := tape ++ List.replicate (head + 1 - List.length tape) 2
        nextConfig = (next, if right then head + 1 else head - 1, List.set padded head symbol)
      | Sum.inr (yes, no) =>
        match readNumeral symbols tape head with
        | Option.none => nextConfig = (no, head, tape)
        | Option.some q =>
          (q ∈ X ∧ nextConfig = (yes, head, tape)) ∨
          (q ∉ X ∧ nextConfig = (no, head, tape))
  let haltsWith (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols) (input : Nat)
      (post : Fin (states + 3) → List (Fin (symbols + 4)) → Prop) : Prop :=
    ∃ (state : Fin (states + 3)) (head : Nat) (tape : List (Fin (symbols + 4))),
      Relation.ReflTransGen (step states symbols program)
        (0, 0, numeral symbols input) (state, head, tape) ∧
      halting states state = true ∧ post state tape
  ( (fun A =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n (fun _ _ => True) ∧
          (haltsWith states symbols program n (fun state _ => state = 1) ↔ n ∈ A)),
    (fun A =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n (fun state _ => state = 1) ↔ n ∈ A),
    (fun f =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n
          (fun _ tape => readNumeral symbols tape 0 = Option.some (f n))) )
RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability.sourceReason: Only the Alphabeta Shared Math Library item https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-relative-computability-and-enumerability states this definition. The article uses relative enumerability without a separate definition. The article-specific portal and the defect report both returned HTTP 404. No correction was available from the report at https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects. The three components express X-computability (Turing reducibility to X), being c.e. in X, and total X-computability. The tape encoding uses a right delimiter, with query numerals beginning at the head and output numerals beginning at cell zero.

AcceptableNumbering.value:
fun φ =>
  let universal := _root_.Partrec₂ φ
  let appendEntry (initialWord entry : _root_.Nat) : _root_.Nat :=
    let place := 2 ^ (_root_.Nat.log2 entry + 1)
    let withLength := initialWord * place + (place - 1)
    withLength * (2 * place) + entry
  (∀ e : _root_.Nat, _root_.Partrec (φ e)) ∧
    (∀ f : _root_.Nat → _root_.Part _root_.Nat, _root_.Partrec f → ∃ e : _root_.Nat, φ e = f) ∧
    universal ∧
    ∃ s : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat, _root_.Computable₂ s ∧
      ∀ e a x : _root_.Nat, φ (s e a) x = φ e (appendEntry (appendEntry 0b1110 a) x)

RigidDegreeAntichain.type:
let rigid := fun A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat =>
  ∀ f : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat, _root_.Computable f →
    (∀ n : _root_.Nat, n ∈ A ↔ f n ∈ A) →
    ∃ N : _root_.Nat, ∀ n : _root_.Nat, N ≤ n → f n = n
let finiteOne := fun A B : _root_.Set _root_.Nat =>
  ∃ f : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat, _root_.Computable f ∧
    (∀ n : _root_.Nat, n ∈ A ↔ f n ∈ B) ∧
    (∀ y : _root_.Nat, _root_.Set.Finite {n : _root_.Nat | f n = y})
let hasAntichain := fun A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat =>
  ∃ B : _root_.Nat → _root_.Set _root_.Nat,
    (∀ i : _root_.Nat,
      _root_.ManyOneReducibilityOnNat (B i) A ∧ _root_.ManyOneReducibilityOnNat A (B i)) ∧
    _root_.Pairwise (fun i j => ¬ finiteOne (B i) (B j) ∧ ¬ finiteOne (B j) (B i))
let asSet := fun a : _root_.Nat → _root_.Bool => {n : _root_.Nat | a n = _root_.Bool.true}
let fairCoin := _root_.MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi
  (fun _ : _root_.Nat =>
    _root_.MeasureTheory.Measure.uniformOfFinset (_root_.Finset.univ : _root_.Finset _root_.Bool))
(∀ A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat, rigid A → hasAntichain A) ∧
  fairCoin {a | rigid (asSet a)} = 1 ∧
  _root_.Filter.Eventually (fun a => rigid (asSet a)) (_root_.residual (_root_.Nat → _root_.Bool)) ∧
  _root_.Filter.Eventually (fun a => hasAntichain (asSet a)) (_root_.MeasureTheory.ae fairCoin) ∧
  _root_.Filter.Eventually (fun a => hasAntichain (asSet a)) (_root_.residual (_root_.Nat → _root_.Bool))

    let p := _root_.Nat.unpair n
    _root_.Part.Dom (φ (_root_.Prod.fst p) (_root_.Prod.snd p))}

    ∀ A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat, sigmaOne A →

PiTwoDescendingCePresentation.type:
∀ P : _root_.Set _root_.Nat,
  {xs : _root_.Fin 1 → _root_.Nat | xs 0 ∈ P} ∈
      (_root_.ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (_root_.Nat.le_succ 1)).2.1 →
  ∃ Q : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → Prop,
    _root_.ComputablePred (fun t : _root_.Nat × _root_.Nat × _root_.Nat =>
      Q t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2) ∧
    (∀ y : _root_.Nat, y ∈ P ↔ ∀ j : _root_.Nat, ∃ s : _root_.Nat, Q y j s) ∧
    (let H (k : _root_.Nat) : _root_.Set _root_.Nat :=
      {y | ∀ j : _root_.Nat, j < k → ∃ s : _root_.Nat, Q y j s}
     let encode (n : _root_.Nat) := _root_.List.replicate n false
     let decode (w : _root_.List _root_.Bool) :=
       if w = encode (_root_.List.length w) then _root_.Option.some (_root_.List.length w)
       else _root_.Option.none
     _root_.ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode
       (_root_.List.replicate_left_injective false)
       (fun n => by simp [decode, encode])
       (fun w hw => _root_.ite_eq_right (fun h => hw ⟨_root_.List.length w, h.symm⟩))
       {z : _root_.Nat | (_root_.Nat.unpair z).2 ∈ H (_root_.Nat.unpair z).1} ∧
     H 0 = _root_.Set.univ ∧ _root_.Antitone H ∧ P = _root_.Set.iInter H)

FixedStageRowStability.type:
∀ φ : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Part _root_.Nat,
  _root_.AcceptableNumbering φ →
  ∀ stage : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Finset _root_.Nat,
    _root_.Computable (fun p : _root_.Nat × _root_.Nat × _root_.Nat =>
      (_root_.Equiv.symm _root_.Finset.equivBitIndices)
        (stage p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)) →
    (∀ e x : _root_.Nat, _root_.Monotone (stage e x)) →
    let V : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Set _root_.Nat :=
      fun e x => {y | ∃ s : _root_.Nat, y ∈ stage e x s}
    (∀ i : _root_.Nat, ∃ e : _root_.Nat, ∀ x y : _root_.Nat,
      y ∈ V e x ↔ _root_.Part.Dom (φ i (_root_.Nat.pair x y))) →
    let K : _root_.Set _root_.Nat := {n |
      let (i, z) := _root_.Nat.unpair n
      _root_.Part.Dom (φ i z)}
    (_root_.RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability K).1 {n |
      let (e, p) := _root_.Nat.unpair n
      let (x, t) := _root_.Nat.unpair p
      ∀ r : _root_.Nat, t ≤ r → stage e x r = stage e x t}
FixedStageRowStability.sourceReason: The endpoint is the fixed-stage oracle decision in the upper-requirement strategy of §4, p. 8, of arXiv:2609.00419v1. The stage sets are finite and increase to their row unions. The exhaustion hypothesis represents the enumeration of all uniformly c.e. families by their paired domains. Stage outputs use binary finite-set codes. The decision takes Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t) as input and uses the paired halting set of the acceptable numbering as the oracle. The article-specific portal and defect report both returned HTTP 404, so no correction could be verified. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=8 https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419 https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects

  (∀ x y : _root_.Nat, y ∈ W x → (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A)) →

  _root_.OneOneReducible

    (fun y : _root_.Nat => y ∈ A)

RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability.proof:
fun X =>
  let Program (states symbols : Nat) :=
    Fin (states + 3) →
      Sum (Fin (symbols + 4) → Fin (states + 3) × Fin (symbols + 4) × Bool)
        (Fin (states + 3) × Fin (states + 3))
  let Configuration (states symbols : Nat) :=
    Fin (states + 3) × Nat × List (Fin (symbols + 4))
  let numeral (symbols n : Nat) : List (Fin (symbols + 4)) :=
    List.map (fun digit => if digit = '0' then 0 else 1) (Nat.toDigits 2 n)
  let readNumeral (symbols : Nat) (tape : List (Fin (symbols + 4))) (start : Nat) :
      Option Nat :=
    let tail := List.drop start tape
    let word := List.takeWhile (fun digit => digit != 3) tail
    let n := List.foldl (fun acc digit => 2 * acc + Fin.val digit) 0 word
    if List.getD tail (List.length word) 2 = 3 ∧ word = numeral symbols n then
      Option.some n
    else
      Option.none
  let halting (states : Nat) (state : Fin (states + 3)) : Bool :=
    state == 1 || state == 2
  let step (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols)
      (config nextConfig : Configuration states symbols) : Prop :=
    let (state, head, tape) := config
    halting states state = false ∧
      match program state with
      | Sum.inl ordinary =>
        let (next, symbol, right) := ordinary (List.getD tape head 2)
        let padded := tape ++ List.replicate (head + 1 - List.length tape) 2
        nextConfig = (next, if right then head + 1 else head - 1, List.set padded head symbol)
      | Sum.inr (yes, no) =>
        match readNumeral symbols tape head with
        | Option.none => nextConfig = (no, head, tape)
        | Option.some q =>
          (q ∈ X ∧ nextConfig = (yes, head, tape)) ∨
          (q ∉ X ∧ nextConfig = (no, head, tape))
  let haltsWith (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols) (input : Nat)
      (post : Fin (states + 3) → List (Fin (symbols + 4)) → Prop) : Prop :=
    ∃ (state : Fin (states + 3)) (head : Nat) (tape : List (Fin (symbols + 4))),
      Relation.ReflTransGen (step states symbols program)
        (0, 0, numeral symbols input) (state, head, tape) ∧
      halting states state = true ∧ post state tape
  ( (fun A =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n (fun _ _ => True) ∧
          (haltsWith states symbols program n (fun state _ => state = 1) ↔ n ∈ A)),
    (fun A =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n (fun state _ => state = 1) ↔ n ∈ A),
    (fun f =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n
          (fun _ tape => readNumeral symbols tape 0 = Option.some (f n))) )

Alphabeta Math's `lem-finite-tuples-admit-effective-prefix-free-encodings`,

and the numeral. This length is one for zero, as required by the linked

forward map, so the Lean proof implements these appends by arithmetic.

The coordinator's bounded scan is furnished by `Primrec.nat_findGreatest`.

recursion. For a downstream application of `Nat.Partrec.Code.smn`, compose

supplier’s evaluation identity.

theorem AcceptableNumbering.computable₂_sequenceCode :
    let appendEntry (initialWord entry : Nat) : Nat :=
      let place := 2 ^ (Nat.log2 entry + 1)
      let withLength := initialWord * place + (place - 1)
      withLength * (2 * place) + entry
    Computable₂ (fun a x => appendEntry (appendEntry 0b1110 a) x) := by
  intro appendEntry
  have power : Primrec₂ ((· ^ ·) : Nat → Nat → Nat) :=
    Primrec₂.unpaired'.1 Nat.Primrec.pow
  have powerTwo : Primrec (fun k : Nat => 2 ^ k) :=
    power.comp (Primrec.const 2) Primrec.id
  have logTwo : Primrec Nat.log2 := by
    have powerTest : PrimrecRel (fun n k : Nat => 2 ^ k ≤ n) :=
      Primrec.nat_le.comp (powerTwo.comp Primrec.snd) Primrec.fst

    intro n
    rcases eq_or_ne n 0 with rfl | hn

    -- The exponent lies in the scan range and no larger exponent passes.

      ⟨Nat.log2_le_self n, fun _ => Nat.log2_self_le hn,
        fun _ hk _ => not_le_of_gt ((Nat.log2_lt hn).1 hk)⟩
  have place : Primrec (fun entry : Nat => 2 ^ (entry.log2 + 1)) :=
    powerTwo.comp (Primrec.succ.comp logTwo)

    change Primrec (fun p : Nat × Nat => appendEntry p.1 p.2)
    have p := place.comp (Primrec.snd : Primrec (Prod.snd : Nat × Nat → Nat))

/- The reviewed definition is the range characterization from
   https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-computably-enumerable-set (Definition).
   This support connects its constant-bit encodings of Nat with mathlib's REPred.

   at https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable. -/
namespace ComputablyEnumerableSet

/-- Both constant-bit unary encodings of Nat are computable. -/
theorem computable_replicate (bit : Bool) :
    Computable (fun n : ℕ => List.replicate n bit) := by
  have hstep : Computable₂ (fun (_ : ℕ) (p : ℕ × List Bool) => bit :: p.2) :=
    (Computable.list_cons.comp (Computable.const bit)
      (Computable.snd.comp Computable.snd)).to₂
  refine (Computable.nat_rec Computable.id (Computable.const ([] : List Bool))
    hstep).of_eq ?_
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ]
    exact congrArg (List.cons bit) ih

/-- Search the indices of a total computable enumeration to recognize its range. -/
theorem nat_rePred_range {e : ℕ → ℕ} (he : Computable e) :
    REPred (fun x => x ∈ Set.range e) := by
  -- In thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable, step 1.1, each equality test terminates.
  -- Here rfind searches the indices directly using equality on Nat.
  have htest : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => decide (e p.2 = p.1)) :=
    Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp (he.comp Computable.snd) Computable.fst
  have hsearch : Partrec (fun x => Nat.rfind (fun n => Part.some (decide (e n = x)))) :=
    Partrec.rfind htest.partrec
  refine hsearch.dom_re.of_eq fun x => ?_
  exact (Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun n => Part.some (decide (e n = x)))).trans
    (by simp [Set.mem_range])

/-- Code representation of a semidecider for membership in a set of Nat. -/
theorem nat_rePred_iff_exists_code (A : Set ℕ) :
    REPred (fun x => x ∈ A) ↔
      ∃ c : Nat.Partrec.Code, ∀ x, (c.eval x).Dom ↔ x ∈ A := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    -- The REPred witness returns Unit. Map its output to 0 for the Nat code.
    have hzero : Partrec (fun x : ℕ =>
        (Part.assert (x ∈ A) (fun _ => Part.some (0 : ℕ)))) := by
      unfold REPred at h
      refine (h.map ((Computable.const (0 : ℕ) : Computable (fun _ : ℕ × Unit => 0)).to₂)).of_eq ?_
      intro x
      ext n
      simp [eq_comm]
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mp (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hzero)
    exact ⟨c, fun x => by
      rw [hc]
      simp [Part.dom_iff_mem]⟩
  · rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
    have h : Nat.Partrec c.eval := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mpr ⟨c, rfl⟩
    exact (Partrec.nat_iff.mpr h).dom_re.of_eq hc

/-- A nonempty c.e. set of Nat is the range of a total computable function. -/
theorem nat_exists_computable_range {A : Set ℕ}
    (hA : REPred (fun x => x ∈ A)) (hne : A.Nonempty) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℕ, Computable e ∧ Set.range e = A := by
  -- thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable, step 1.2 supplies a fallback member;
  -- we choose one from nonemptiness and use it as a computable constant.
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (nat_rePred_iff_exists_code A).mp hA
  -- Step 2.1 uses shortlex words. For Nat, unpair the input into a candidate
  -- and fuel. This specializes the bounded-code construction in Tau Ceti
  -- REPred.exists_computable_range at revision 91942aa9ff8cea04d0d9905b80f75c07ce2379c4
  -- to Nat using only the pinned mathlib modules.
  let bounded (n : ℕ) := Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln n.unpair.2 c n.unpair.1
  let e (n : ℕ) : ℕ := if (bounded n).isSome then n.unpair.1 else a
  have hinput : Computable (fun n => (Nat.unpair n).1) :=
    Computable.fst.comp Computable.unpair
  have hfuel : Computable (fun n => (Nat.unpair n).2) :=
    Computable.snd.comp Computable.unpair
  have hbounded : Computable bounded :=
    Nat.Partrec.Code.primrec_evaln.to_comp.comp
      ((hfuel.pair (Computable.const c)).pair hinput)
  have he : Computable e := by
    simpa only [e, Bool.cond_eq_ite] using
      (Primrec.option_isSome.to_comp.comp hbounded).cond hinput (Computable.const a)
  have hcovered (x : ℕ) : x ∈ A ↔ ∃ t, (Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln t c x).isSome := by
    rw [← hc x, Part.dom_iff_mem]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨out, hout⟩
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete.mp hout
      exact ⟨t, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mpr ⟨out, ht⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
      obtain ⟨out, hout⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp ht
      exact ⟨out, Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete.mpr ⟨t, hout⟩⟩
  refine ⟨e, he, Set.ext fun x => ?_⟩
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl⟩
    by_cases h : (bounded n).isSome
    · rw [show e n = n.unpair.1 from ite_eq_left h]
      exact (hcovered _).mpr ⟨n.unpair.2, h⟩
    · rw [show e n = a from ite_eq_right h]
      exact ha
  · intro hx
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := (hcovered x).mp hx
    exact ⟨Nat.pair x t, by simp [e, bounded, ht]⟩

/-- Nat bridge for the raw reviewed definition, which follows this support. -/
theorem nat_rePred_iff (bit : Bool) (A : Set ℕ) :
    REPred (fun x => x ∈ A) ↔
      A = ∅ ∨ ∃ e : ℕ → ℕ,
        Computable (fun n : ℕ => List.replicate (e n) bit) ∧ Set.range e = A := by
  -- Step 3.1 combines the directions. Both directions treat the empty set
  -- separately, since a total map out of Nat always has some output.
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_cases he : A = ∅
    · exact Or.inl he
    · obtain ⟨e, hc, hr⟩ := nat_exists_computable_range h (Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr he)
      exact Or.inr ⟨e, (computable_replicate bit).comp hc, hr⟩
  · rintro (rfl | ⟨e, he, rfl⟩)
    · exact (Partrec.none (α := ℕ) (σ := ℕ)).dom_re.of_eq fun x => by simp
    · apply nat_rePred_range
      exact (Computable.list_length.comp he).of_eq fun n => List.length_replicate

end ComputablyEnumerableSet

InfiniteHomogeneousRows.proof:
by
  intro A W encode decode hce hhom hinfinite
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §3, pp. 4–5, uses the computable
  -- enumeration of pairs without repetition. Here stage k treats Nat.unpair k.
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect report returned HTTP 404.
  -- The reviewed c.e. supplier gives a domain code for the packed row graph.
  -- A single successful bounded evaluation certifies a row member.
  -- Thus the search can range over candidate and fuel codes in Nat order.
  let graph : Set ℕ := {z | ∃ x y : ℕ, y ∈ W x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y}
  have hgraph : REPred (fun z => z ∈ graph) :=
    (ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff true graph).mpr hce
  obtain ⟨code, hcode⟩ :=
    (ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff_exists_code graph).mp hgraph
  have hstage (x y : ℕ) :
      y ∈ W x ↔ ∃ fuel, (code.evaln fuel (Nat.pair x y)).isSome := by
    have hpair : Nat.pair x y ∈ graph ↔ y ∈ W x := by
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨row, value, hmem, heq⟩
        have hxy : (x, y) = (row, value) := by
          simpa only [Nat.unpair_pair] using congrArg Nat.unpair heq
        cases hxy
        exact hmem
      · intro hmem
        exact ⟨x, y, hmem, rfl⟩
    rw [← hpair, ← hcode, Part.dom_iff_mem]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨out, hout⟩
      obtain ⟨fuel, hfuel⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete.mp hout
      exact ⟨fuel, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mpr ⟨out, hfuel⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨fuel, hfuel⟩
      obtain ⟨out, hout⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp hfuel
      exact ⟨out, Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete.mpr ⟨fuel, hout⟩⟩

  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations
  -- steps 1.1 and 3.1 motivate keeping the earlier outputs and using infinitude
  -- for termination. Here the required row varies with the input, so search
  -- jointly for a candidate and enough fuel to certify its row membership.
  let bounded (p : (ℕ × List ℕ) × ℕ) :=
    code.evaln p.2.unpair.2 (Nat.pair p.1.1.unpair.1 p.2.unpair.1)
  let eligible (state : ℕ × List ℕ) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
    (bounded (state, k)).isSome ∧ k.unpair.1 ∉ state.2
  let : DecidableRel eligible := fun state k => by
    unfold eligible
    infer_instance
  have hrow : Computable (fun p : (ℕ × List ℕ) × ℕ => p.1.1.unpair.1) :=
    Computable.fst.comp (Primrec.unpair.to_comp.comp (Computable.fst.comp Computable.fst))
  have hcandidate : Computable (fun p : (ℕ × List ℕ) × ℕ => p.2.unpair.1) :=
    Computable.fst.comp (Primrec.unpair.to_comp.comp Computable.snd)
  have hfuel : Computable (fun p : (ℕ × List ℕ) × ℕ => p.2.unpair.2) :=
    Computable.snd.comp (Primrec.unpair.to_comp.comp Computable.snd)
  have hbounded : Computable bounded :=
    Nat.Partrec.Code.primrec_evaln.to_comp.comp
      ((hfuel.pair (Computable.const code)).pair (Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp hrow hcandidate))
  have hmem : PrimrecRel (fun (xs : List ℕ) (y : ℕ) => y ∈ xs) :=
    (PrimrecRel.exists_mem_list (R := @Eq ℕ) Primrec.eq).of_eq (by intro xs y; simp)
  have heligible : ComputablePred (fun p : (ℕ × List ℕ) × ℕ => eligible p.1 p.2) := by
    apply Computable.computablePred
    refine (Primrec.and.to_comp.comp (Primrec.option_isSome.to_comp.comp hbounded)
      (hmem.not.decide.to_comp.comp (Computable.snd.comp Computable.fst) hcandidate)).of_eq ?_
    intro p
    simp [eligible]
  have hexists (state : ℕ × List ℕ) : ∃ k, eligible state k := by
    obtain ⟨y, hy, hnew⟩ := (hinfinite state.1.unpair.1).exists_notMem_finset state.2.toFinset
    obtain ⟨fuel, hfound⟩ := (hstage _ _).mp hy
    have hnotUsed : y ∉ state.2 := by simpa using hnew
    exact ⟨Nat.pair y fuel, by simpa [eligible, bounded] using And.intro hfound hnotUsed⟩
  let choose (state : ℕ × List ℕ) := (Nat.find (hexists state)).unpair.1
  have hchoose : Computable choose :=
    (Computable.fst.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp).comp (Computable.find heligible hexists)
  have hchosen (state : ℕ × List ℕ) :
      choose state ∈ W state.1.unpair.1 ∧ choose state ∉ state.2 := by
    have hs := Nat.find_spec (hexists state)
    exact ⟨(hstage _ _).mpr ⟨(Nat.find (hexists state)).unpair.2, hs.1⟩, hs.2⟩

  let history (n : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
    Nat.rec [] (fun k xs => choose (k, xs) :: xs) n
  have hstep : Computable₂ (fun (_ : ℕ) (p : ℕ × List ℕ) => choose p :: p.2) :=
    (Computable.list_cons.comp (hchoose.comp Computable.snd)
      (Computable.snd.comp Computable.snd)).to₂
  have hhistory : Computable history :=
    Computable.nat_rec Computable.id (Computable.const ([] : List ℕ)) hstep
  let f (n : ℕ) := choose (n, history n)
  have hf : Computable f := hchoose.comp (Computable.id.pair hhistory)
  -- Step 2.1 uses freshness for injectivity. Every earlier output belongs to
  -- the current history. Surjectivity onto a row is unnecessary here.
  have hearlier (i j : ℕ) (hij : i < j) : f i ∈ history j := by
    induction j with
    | zero => omega
    | succ j ih =>
      change f i ∈ f j :: history j
      rcases lt_or_eq_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt_succ hij) with hlt | rfl
      · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (ih hlt)
      · exact List.mem_cons_self
  have hne (i j : ℕ) (hij : i < j) : f i ≠ f j := by
    intro heq
    apply (hchosen (j, history j)).2
    change f j ∈ history j
    rw [← heq]
    exact hearlier i j hij
  refine ⟨f, hf, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i j heq
    rcases lt_trichotomy i j with hlt | he | hgt
    · exact (hne i j hlt heq).elim
    · exact he
    · exact (hne j i hgt heq.symm).elim
  · intro z
    have hcyl : (∃ x n : ℕ, x ∈ A ∧ z = Nat.pair x n) ↔ z.unpair.1 ∈ A := by
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨x, n, hx, rfl⟩
        simpa only [Nat.unpair_pair] using hx
      · intro hx
        exact ⟨z.unpair.1, z.unpair.2, hx, (Nat.pair_unpair z).symm⟩
    exact hcyl.trans (hhom _ _ (hchosen (z, history z)).1).symm

FiniteInjuryAndStabilization.proof:
by
  classical
  intro φ V rowAt pairBefore chosenPair satisfied content marker
    upper lower acts injured restraints upperCandidate lowerCandidate
    _effectiveFunctions _allPartialComputable _effectiveFamilies _allUniformCEFamilies
    _computableStages _increasingStages _stageUnions _pairOrder _computablePairOrder
    _initial nextStage _activeMarkers eligible permanent upperVisit lowerVisit
  /- Source: arXiv:2609.00419v1, §4, p. 9, unnumbered Verification.
     The article's Research Portal and designated defect-report routes both returned
     HTTP 404, and there is no verified numbered Alphabeta proof for this endpoint.
     The comments follow the paragraphs of the article's Verification. -/
  -- Verification, paragraph 1: check the exact visit at which a live marker changes.
  -- The visit equations incorporate row disjointness and cancellation order.
  have visitEffect (s k e m : ℕ) (visit : k < s) (live : marker s k e = some m) :
      marker s (k + 1) e = some m ∨
        (marker s (k + 1) e = none ∧
          ∃ i q, k = upper i ∧ upper i < lower e ∧ chosenPair s i = some q ∧
            m ∈ rowAt i q.1 q.2) := by
    have kind : k = upper (k / 2) ∨ k = lower (k / 2) := by
      dsimp [upper, lower]
      omega
    rcases kind with upperIndex | lowerIndex
    · let i := k / 2
      have atUpper : upper i < s := upperIndex ▸ visit
      have step := upperVisit s i atUpper
      rw [upperIndex]
      cases selected : chosenPair s i with
      | none =>
        simp only [selected] at step
        exact Or.inl ((step.2.2 e).trans (upperIndex ▸ live))
      | some q =>
        simp only [selected] at step
        have before : marker s (upper i) e = some m := upperIndex ▸ live
        have after := step.2.2.2 e
        rw [before] at after
        by_cases cancels : upper i < lower e ∧ m ∈ rowAt i q.1 q.2
        · exact Or.inr ⟨by simpa [cancels] using after, i, q, rfl, cancels.1, selected, cancels.2⟩
        · exact Or.inl (by simpa [cancels] using after)
    · let j := k / 2
      have atLower : lower j < s := lowerIndex ▸ visit
      have step := lowerVisit s j atLower
      rw [lowerIndex]
      left
      by_cases same : e = j
      · subst e
        have before : marker s (lower j) j = some m := lowerIndex ▸ live
        have after := step.2.2
        simpa only [before] using after
      · exact (step.2.1 e same).trans (lowerIndex ▸ live)

  have cause (s k e : ℕ) (event : injured s k e) :
      ∃ i q m, k = upper i ∧ upper i < lower e ∧
        chosenPair s i = some q ∧ marker s k e = some m ∧ m ∈ rowAt i q.1 q.2 := by
    obtain ⟨visit, ⟨m, live⟩, cancelled⟩ := event
    rcases visitEffect s k e m visit live with kept | ⟨_, i, q, hi, priority, selected, mem⟩
    · rw [cancelled] at kept
      cases kept
    · exact ⟨i, q, m, hi, priority, selected, live, mem⟩

  -- Verification, paragraphs 2–3: satisfaction persists from the stage immediately
  -- after an action. Eligibility then rules out a second action at any later stage.
  have satisfiedLater (i s : ℕ) (action : acts s i) (t : ℕ) (later : s < t) :
      satisfied t i := by
    have later' : s + 1 ≤ t := later
    clear later
    induction t, later' using Nat.le_induction with
    | base => exact (permanent s i).mpr (Or.inr action)
    | succ t _ ih => exact (permanent t i).mpr (Or.inl ih)
  have once (i s t : ℕ) (first : acts s i) (second : acts t i) : s = t := by
    rcases lt_trichotomy s t with earlier | same | later
    · exact ((eligible t i second).2 (satisfiedLater i s first t earlier)).elim
    · exact same
    · exact ((eligible s i first).2 (satisfiedLater i t second s later)).elim

  exact ⟨cause, once, FiniteInjuryAndStabilization.of_trace acts marker
    (fun s e => (nextStage s).2 e) once
    (fun s k e m visit live cancelled => by
      obtain ⟨i, q, _, hi, priority, selected, _, _⟩ :=
        cause s k e ⟨visit, ⟨m, live⟩, cancelled⟩
      exact ⟨i, hi, priority, q, selected⟩)
    (fun s k e m visit live => by
      rcases visitEffect s k e m visit live with kept | ⟨cancelled, _⟩
      · exact Or.inr kept
      · exact Or.inl cancelled)⟩
FiniteInjuryAndStabilization.support:
namespace FiniteInjuryAndStabilization

/-- The marker part of the finite-injury argument in §4, p. 9.
It applies to any lower search whose visits never replace a live marker. -/
theorem of_trace
    (acts : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) (marker : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Option ℕ)
    (nextStage : ∀ s e, marker (s + 1) 0 e = marker s s e)
    (once : ∀ i s t, acts s i → acts t i → s = t)
    (cause : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s k e = some m →
      marker s (k + 1) e = none → ∃ i, k = 2 * i ∧ 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 ∧ acts s i)
    (noReplacement : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s k e = some m →
      marker s (k + 1) e = none ∨ marker s (k + 1) e = some m) :
    let injured (s k e : ℕ) : Prop :=
      k < s ∧ (∃ m, marker s k e = some m) ∧ marker s (k + 1) e = none
    let restraints (s k p : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
      {m | ∃ e, 2 * e + 1 < p ∧ marker s k e = some m}
    (∀ e, Set.Finite {event : ℕ × ℕ | injured event.1 event.2 e}) ∧
    (∀ e, ∃ s₀,
      (∀ s i, s₀ < s → 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 → ¬ acts s i) ∧
      (∀ s k, s₀ < s → ¬ injured s k e) ∧
      (∀ m s k, marker s₀ s₀ e = some m →
        s₀ < s → k ≤ s → marker s k e = some m)) ∧
    (∀ e, ∃ s₁ final, ∀ s k, s₁ ≤ s → k ≤ s → marker s k e = final) ∧
    (∀ p, ∃ (s₁ : ℕ) (Z : Set ℕ), Z.Finite ∧
      ∀ s k, s₁ ≤ s → k ≤ s → restraints s k p = Z) := by
  classical
  intro injured restraints
  have stageBound {α : Type} (S : Set α) (finite : S.Finite) (stage : α → ℕ) :
      ∃ bound, ∀ a ∈ S, stage a ≤ bound := by
    by_cases nonempty : finite.toFinset.Nonempty
    · obtain ⟨a, _, maximal⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image finite.toFinset stage nonempty
      exact ⟨stage a, fun b hb => maximal b (finite.mem_toFinset.mpr hb)⟩
    · have empty := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp nonempty
      refine ⟨0, fun a ha => ?_⟩
      have mem := finite.mem_toFinset.mpr ha
      simp [empty] at mem

  -- Verification, paragraphs 1–3 (p. 9): charge each cancellation to its upper visit.
  -- The stage/visit pairs already identify actual cancellations. The two reviewed Tau Ceti
  -- suppliers use fresh entries at or below a restraint and a union of injuring numbers
  -- (Causes.lean:58 and Basic.lean:259 at 91942aa9ff8cea04d0d9905b80f75c07ce2379c4).
  -- Such a batch can be nonempty without the marker being cancelled. Here the finite graph
  -- of actual upper actions bounds both cancellation events and their stages directly.
  let higherActions (e : ℕ) : Set (ℕ × ℕ) :=
    {a | 2 * a.2 < 2 * e + 1 ∧ acts a.1 a.2}
  have finiteActions (e : ℕ) : (higherActions e).Finite := by
    have injective : Set.InjOn Prod.snd (higherActions e) := by
      rintro ⟨s, i⟩ hs ⟨t, j⟩ ht (rfl : i = j)
      exact Prod.ext (once i s t hs.2 ht.2) rfl
    apply (Set.finite_image_iff injective).mp
    apply (Set.finite_le_nat e).subset
    rintro _ ⟨⟨s, i⟩, hi, rfl⟩
    have priority : 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 := hi.1
    change i ≤ e
    omega
  have finiteInjuries (e : ℕ) : Set.Finite {a : ℕ × ℕ | injured a.1 a.2 e} := by
    apply ((finiteActions e).image (fun a => (a.1, 2 * a.2))).subset
    rintro ⟨s, k⟩ ⟨visit, ⟨m, before⟩, after⟩
    obtain ⟨i, rfl, priority, action⟩ := cause s k e m visit before after
    exact ⟨(s, i), ⟨priority, action⟩, rfl⟩
  have noLateActions (e : ℕ) :
      ∃ s₀, ∀ s i, s₀ < s → 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 → ¬ acts s i := by
    obtain ⟨s₀, bound⟩ := stageBound (higherActions e) (finiteActions e) Prod.fst
    exact ⟨s₀, fun s i late priority action =>
      (Nat.not_le_of_lt late) (bound (s, i) ⟨priority, action⟩)⟩
  have afterBound (e s₀ : ℕ)
      (noAction : ∀ s i, s₀ < s → 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 → ¬ acts s i) :
      (∀ s k, s₀ < s → ¬ injured s k e) ∧
      (∀ m s k, marker s₀ s₀ e = some m →
        s₀ < s → k ≤ s → marker s k e = some m) ∧
      (∃ s₁ final, ∀ s k, s₁ ≤ s → k ≤ s → marker s k e = final) := by
    have noInjury (s k : ℕ) (late : s₀ < s) : ¬ injured s k e := by
      rintro ⟨visit, ⟨m, before⟩, after⟩
      obtain ⟨i, _, priority, action⟩ := cause s k e m visit before after
      exact noAction s i late priority action

    -- Verification, paragraph 4: propagate a live marker through individual visits,
    -- then across the stage boundary. The first persistence argument starts at
    -- the *end* of the bound stage, as required by the stage/visit convention.
    have throughVisits (m s k : ℕ) (late : s₀ < s)
        (live : marker s k e = some m) (j : ℕ) (fromVisit : k ≤ j) (valid : j ≤ s) :
        marker s j e = some m := by
      induction j, fromVisit using Nat.le_induction with
      | base => exact live
      | succ j _ ih =>
        have visit : j < s := by omega
        have before := ih (Nat.le_of_lt visit)
        rcases noReplacement s j e m visit before with after | after
        · exact (noInjury s j late ⟨visit, ⟨m, before⟩, after⟩).elim
        · exact after
    have carryLater (m r : ℕ) (pastBound : s₀ ≤ r) (live : marker r r e = some m)
        (s : ℕ) (later : r < s) : ∀ k ≤ s, marker s k e = some m := by
      have later' : r + 1 ≤ s := later
      clear later
      induction s, later' using Nat.le_induction with
      | base =>
        intro k valid
        exact throughVisits m (r + 1) 0 (by omega)
          ((nextStage r e).trans live) k (Nat.zero_le k) valid
      | succ s _ ih =>
        intro k valid
        exact throughVisits m (s + 1) 0 (by omega)
          ((nextStage s e).trans (ih s le_rfl)) k (Nat.zero_le k) valid
    refine ⟨noInjury, fun m s k live late valid => carryLater m s₀ le_rfl live s late k valid, ?_⟩
    by_cases laterMarker : ∃ s k m, s₀ < s ∧ k ≤ s ∧ marker s k e = some m
    · obtain ⟨s, k, m, late, valid, live⟩ := laterMarker
      have endLive := throughVisits m s k late live s valid le_rfl
      -- Any later live visit supplies a bound, so no least allocation stage is needed.
      exact ⟨s + 1, some m, fun t j ht hj =>
        carryLater m s (Nat.le_of_lt late) endLive t ht j hj⟩
    · refine ⟨s₀ + 1, none, fun s k late valid => ?_⟩
      cases seen : marker s k e with
      | none => rfl
      | some m => exact (laterMarker ⟨s, k, m, late, valid, seen⟩).elim

  have quiet (e : ℕ) : ∃ s₀,
      (∀ s i, s₀ < s → 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 → ¬ acts s i) ∧
      (∀ s k, s₀ < s → ¬ injured s k e) ∧
      (∀ m s k, marker s₀ s₀ e = some m →
        s₀ < s → k ≤ s → marker s k e = some m) := by
    obtain ⟨s₀, noAction⟩ := noLateActions e
    exact ⟨s₀, noAction, (afterBound e s₀ noAction).1, (afterBound e s₀ noAction).2.1⟩
  have stable (e : ℕ) : ∃ s₁ final, ∀ s k, s₁ ≤ s → k ≤ s → marker s k e = final := by
    obtain ⟨s₀, noAction⟩ := noLateActions e
    exact (afterBound e s₀ noAction).2.2

  -- Verification, final paragraph: take one bound for the finitely many higher
  -- lower requirements and collect the live values of their final options.
  refine ⟨finiteInjuries, quiet, stable, fun p => ?_⟩
  choose stage value fixed using stable
  let higher : Set ℕ := {e | 2 * e + 1 < p}
  have finiteHigher : higher.Finite := (Set.finite_lt_nat p).subset (by
    intro e h
    change 2 * e + 1 < p at h
    change e < p
    omega)
  obtain ⟨s₁, bound⟩ := stageBound higher finiteHigher stage
  let Z : Set ℕ := {m | ∃ e ∈ higher, value e = some m}
  refine ⟨s₁, Z, ?_, ?_⟩
  · apply (finiteHigher.image (fun e => (value e).getD 0)).subset
    rintro m ⟨e, he, hm⟩
    exact ⟨e, he, by simp [hm]⟩
  · intro s k hs hk
    ext m
    change (∃ e ∈ higher, marker s k e = some m) ↔ ∃ e ∈ higher, value e = some m
    constructor <;> rintro ⟨e, he, hm⟩ <;> refine ⟨e, he, ?_⟩
    · rwa [fixed e s k ((bound e he).trans hs) hk] at hm
    · rwa [fixed e s k ((bound e he).trans hs) hk]

end FiniteInjuryAndStabilization

HaltingSigmaOneCompleteness.proof:
by
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete, Proof.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete
  -- The article-specific Research Portal and defect-report routes returned HTTP 404.
  -- TauCeti's rePred_iff_exists_code and rePred_exists concern REPred.
  -- Here code selection and total Boolean minimization directly connect
  -- the universal partial function and the reviewed primitive-recursive matrix.
  classical
  intro φ hφ K sigmaOne
  obtain ⟨_, hsurj, huniversal, _⟩ := hφ
  have hSigma (A : Set Nat) :
      sigmaOne A ↔ ∃ R : (Fin 1 → Nat) → (Fin 1 → Nat) → Prop,
        PrimrecRel R ∧ ∀ xs : Fin 1 → Nat, xs 0 ∈ A ↔
          ∃ y : Nat, R xs (Fin.cons y Fin.elim0) := by
    rfl
  constructor
  · -- Alphabeta Math, thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete, step 1.1.
    -- Joint partial recursiveness applies after decoding the input pair.
    -- Bounded evaluation of a code gives the required primitive-recursive
    -- matrix directly in the reviewed singleton-tuple encoding.
    have hpacked : Partrec (fun n : Nat => φ n.unpair.1 n.unpair.2) :=
      huniversal.comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.unpair).to_comp
        (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.unpair).to_comp
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mp (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hpacked)
    have hcoord : Primrec (fun xs : Fin 1 → Nat => xs 0) :=
      Primrec.fin_app.comp Primrec.id (Primrec.const 0)
    have htest : Primrec (fun p : (Fin 1 → Nat) × (Fin 1 → Nat) =>
        (Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln (p.2 0) c (p.1 0)).isSome) :=
      Primrec.option_isSome.comp (Nat.Partrec.Code.primrec_evaln.comp
        (((hcoord.comp Primrec.snd).pair (Primrec.const c)).pair (hcoord.comp Primrec.fst)))
    apply (hSigma K).mpr
    refine ⟨fun xs ys => (Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln (ys 0) c (xs 0)).isSome, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact Primrec.eq.comp htest (Primrec.const true)
    · intro xs
      change (φ (xs 0).unpair.1 (xs 0).unpair.2).Dom ↔
        ∃ y : Nat, (Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln y c (xs 0)).isSome = true
      rw [← congrFun hc (xs 0), Part.dom_iff_mem]
      simp only [Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete, Option.isSome_iff_exists, Option.mem_def]
      exact exists_comm
  · -- Step 1.2. Use the given primitive-recursive matrix on singleton
    -- tuples. Minimization is valid because every witness test is total.
    intro A hA
    obtain ⟨R, hR, hmem⟩ := (hSigma A).mp hA
    let singleton (n : Nat) : Fin 1 → Nat := Fin.cons n Fin.elim0
    have hsingleton : Primrec singleton := by
      apply Primrec.fin_curry.mpr
      convert (Primrec₂.left : Primrec₂ (fun n : Nat => fun _ : Fin 1 => n)) using 1
      funext n i
      rw [Fin.eq_zero i]
      rfl
    let P (n y : Nat) := R (singleton n) (singleton y)
    have hP : ComputablePred (fun p : Nat × Nat => P p.1 p.2) :=
      PrimrecPred.computablePred (hR.comp (hsingleton.comp Primrec.fst) (hsingleton.comp Primrec.snd))
    let search (n : Nat) := Nat.rfind (fun y => Part.some (decide (P n y)))
    have hsearch : Partrec search := Partrec.rfind hP.decide.partrec
    have hdom (n : Nat) : (search n).Dom ↔ n ∈ A := by
      rw [show (search n).Dom ↔ ∃ y, P n y from by
        simpa [search] using (Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun y => Part.some (decide (P n y))))]
      exact (hmem (singleton n)).symm
    -- Step 2.1 uses n ↦ ⟨eₙ, 0⟩ after hard-wiring n in step 1.2.
    -- Here surjectivity supplies a single index for the unary search, so
    -- the computable reduction carries n in the input as n ↦ ⟨e, n⟩.
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hsurj search hsearch
    refine ⟨Nat.pair e, Primrec₂.natPair.comp (Primrec.const e) Primrec.id |>.to_comp, ?_⟩
    intro n
    change n ∈ A ↔ (φ (Nat.unpair (Nat.pair e n)).1 (Nat.unpair (Nat.pair e n)).2).Dom
    rw [Nat.unpair_pair, he]
    exact (hdom n).symm
HaltingSigmaOneCompleteness.support:
namespace HaltingSigmaOneCompleteness

/- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §4, p. 8, fixes effective enumerations
   of the partial functions and uniformly c.e. families, with uniformly
   computable increasing finite stages. The canonical enumeration below
   supplies those data. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=8 -/

/-- The numbering of unary partial recursive functions by mathlib codes. -/
noncomputable def canonicalNumbering (e x : Nat) : Part Nat :=
  (Denumerable.ofNat Nat.Partrec.Code e).eval x

theorem canonicalNumbering_acceptable : AcceptableNumbering canonicalNumbering := by
  have huniversal : Partrec₂ canonicalNumbering := by
    change Partrec (fun p : Nat × Nat => (Denumerable.ofNat Nat.Partrec.Code p.1).eval p.2)
    exact Nat.Partrec.Code.eval_part.comp ((Computable.ofNat _).comp Computable.fst) Computable.snd
  refine ⟨fun e => huniversal.comp (Computable.const e) Computable.id, ?_, huniversal, ?_⟩
  · intro f hf
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mp (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hf)
    refine ⟨Encodable.encode c, ?_⟩
    unfold canonicalNumbering
    rw [Denumerable.ofNat_encode, hc]
  · -- Code.smn expects Nat.pair on its input. Compute the reviewed
    -- two-entry sequence code before calling the original evaluator.
    let G (n : Nat) : Part Nat :=
      let e := n.unpair.1.unpair.1
      let a := n.unpair.1.unpair.2
      let x := n.unpair.2
      let appendEntry (initialWord entry : Nat) : Nat :=
        let place := 2 ^ (Nat.log2 entry + 1)
        let withLength := initialWord * place + (place - 1)
        withLength * (2 * place) + entry
      canonicalNumbering e (appendEntry (appendEntry 0b1110 a) x)
    have hleft : Computable (fun n : Nat => n.unpair.1.unpair) :=
      Primrec.unpair.to_comp.comp ((Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.unpair).to_comp)
    have hG : Partrec G :=
      huniversal.comp (Computable.fst.comp hleft)
        (AcceptableNumbering.computable₂_sequenceCode.comp (Computable.snd.comp hleft)
          (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.unpair).to_comp)
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mp (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hG)
    obtain ⟨specialize, hspecialize, heval⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.smn
    refine ⟨fun e a => Encodable.encode (specialize c (Nat.pair e a)), ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact Computable.encode.comp₂
        (hspecialize.comp₂ (Computable.const c) Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp)
    · intro e a x
      simp only [canonicalNumbering, Denumerable.ofNat_encode, heval, hc, G, Nat.unpair_pair]

/-- The row of the c.e. graph coded by e at x. -/
def row (e x : Nat) : Set Nat :=
  {y | (canonicalNumbering e (Nat.pair x y)).Dom}

/-- At stage s, retain y < s for which the packed input halts with fuel s. -/
def rowAt (e x s : Nat) : Finset Nat :=
  (Finset.range s).filter (fun y =>
    (Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln s (Denumerable.ofNat Nat.Partrec.Code e) (Nat.pair x y)).isSome)

theorem monotone_rowAt (e x : Nat) : Monotone (rowAt e x) := by
  intro s t hst y
  simp only [rowAt, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Option.isSome_iff_exists]
  rintro ⟨hy, z, hz⟩
  exact ⟨lt_of_lt_of_le hy hst, z, Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_mono hst hz⟩

theorem mem_row_iff_exists_stage (e x y : Nat) :
    y ∈ row e x ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ rowAt e x s := by
  change (Nat.Partrec.Code.eval (Denumerable.ofNat Nat.Partrec.Code e) (Nat.pair x y)).Dom ↔ _
  simp only [Part.dom_iff_mem, Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete, rowAt, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_range, Option.isSome_iff_exists]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨z, s, hz⟩
    exact ⟨max s (y + 1), lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self y) (le_max_right _ _), z,
      Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_mono (le_max_left _ _) hz⟩
  · rintro ⟨s, _, z, hz⟩
    exact ⟨z, s, hz⟩

/--
The binary code is a bounded sum over y, keeping e, x and the fuel s fixed
throughout the recursion. TauCeti's optional domStage suppliers operate on
unary code inputs. These stages evaluate the paired input and sum powers
with exponent y directly, producing row codes on the required triple.
-/
theorem computable_rowAt_code :
    Computable (fun p : Nat × Nat × Nat => Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (rowAt p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)) := by
  let test (p : Nat × Nat × Nat) (y : Nat) : Bool :=
    (Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln p.2.2 (Denumerable.ofNat Nat.Partrec.Code p.1)
      (Nat.pair p.2.1 y)).isSome
  have htest : Primrec₂ test := by
    change Primrec (fun q : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Nat => test q.1 q.2)
    have fuel : Primrec (fun q : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Nat => q.1.2.2) :=
      Primrec.snd.comp (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.fst)
    have code : Primrec (fun q : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Nat =>
        Denumerable.ofNat Nat.Partrec.Code q.1.1) :=
      (Primrec.ofNat _).comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.fst)
    have input : Primrec (fun q : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Nat => Nat.pair q.1.2.1 q.2) :=
      Primrec₂.natPair.comp (Primrec.fst.comp (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.fst)) Primrec.snd
    exact Primrec.option_isSome.comp (Nat.Partrec.Code.primrec_evaln.comp ((fuel.pair code).pair input))
  let term (p : Nat × Nat × Nat) (y : Nat) : Nat := bif test p y then 2 ^ y else 0
  have hterm : Primrec₂ term := by
    change Primrec (fun q : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Nat => term q.1 q.2)
    have pow : Primrec₂ ((· ^ ·) : Nat → Nat → Nat) :=
      Primrec₂.unpaired'.mp Nat.Primrec.pow
    exact Primrec.cond htest (pow.comp (Primrec.const 2) Primrec.snd) (Primrec.const 0)
  have hstep : Primrec₂ (fun (p : Nat × Nat × Nat) (q : Nat × Nat) => q.2 + term p q.1) :=
    Primrec.nat_add.comp (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.snd)
      (hterm.comp Primrec.fst (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.snd))
  have hsum (p : Nat × Nat × Nat) (k : Nat) :
      Nat.rec 0 (fun y acc => acc + term p y) k = ∑ y ∈ Finset.range k, term p y := by
    induction k with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k ih =>
      change Nat.rec 0 (fun y acc => acc + term p y) k + term p k = _
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, ih]
  refine (Primrec.nat_rec' (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.snd) (Primrec.const 0) hstep).to_comp.of_eq ?_
  intro p
  rw [hsum, Finset.equivBitIndices_symm_apply, rowAt, Finset.sum_filter]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by cases test p y <;> simp [term, test, *]

/-- Each numbered partial domain occurs among the unions of stage rows. -/
theorem rowAt_exhausts_numbering (i : Nat) :
    ∃ e : Nat, ∀ x y : Nat, (∃ s, y ∈ rowAt e x s) ↔
      (canonicalNumbering i (Nat.pair x y)).Dom :=
  ⟨i, fun x y => (mem_row_iff_exists_stage i x y).symm⟩

/-- Every c.e. predicate of packed pairs is exhausted by a single index. -/
theorem exists_index_stages {P : Nat → Prop} (hP : REPred P) :
    ∃ e : Nat, ∀ x y : Nat, P (Nat.pair x y) ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ rowAt e x s := by
  -- A total continuation replaces the semidecider's Unit output with 0.
  -- The domain is preserved, so code selection applies to a Nat output.
  let f (n : Nat) := (Part.assert (P n) (fun _ => Part.some ())).bind (fun _ => Part.some (0 : Nat))
  have hf : Partrec f := Partrec.bind hP (Computable.const (0 : Nat)).partrec
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mp (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hf)
  refine ⟨Encodable.encode c, fun x y => (Iff.trans ?_ (mem_row_iff_exists_stage _ x y))⟩
  change P (Nat.pair x y) ↔ (canonicalNumbering (Encodable.encode c) (Nat.pair x y)).Dom
  by_cases h : P (Nat.pair x y) <;> simp [canonicalNumbering, hc, f, Part.assert_pos, Part.assert_neg, h]

end HaltingSigmaOneCompleteness

external.usage: Compose joint evaluation on (Code, Nat) with the computable Nat-to-Code enumeration to obtain joint partial recursiveness of the canonical numbering.
Select a code for the packed universal map in step 1.1, for each partial function and the joint specialization preprocessor in the canonical numbering, and for the semidecider of a packed row graph.
Use primitive-recursive bounded evaluation to test the Σ₁ matrix and the candidates in the uniformly computable finite row stages.
Turn convergence into a finite fuel witness and bounded success into convergence, both for the Σ₁ matrix and for the union of the row stages.
Obtain one unary partial-recursive search by minimizing the total Boolean test for the primitive-recursive witness matrix.
The search halts exactly when the matrix holds for some witness, since the Boolean test is defined at every smaller candidate.
Hard-wire the packed pair (e,a) into the code for the joint evaluator after composing the evaluator with the reviewed two-entry sequence encoder.
Preserve bounded halting when the fuel increases, both in monotonicity of the stages and in choosing a stage large enough to include the row coordinate.

PiTwoDescendingCePresentation.proof:
by
  classical
  intro P hP
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §2, p. 3, proof of Lemma 1.
  -- The source starts with a computable matrix. The reviewed hierarchy
  -- definition supplies the primitive-recursive matrix of the complement,
  -- so expand its tuple quantifiers and negate the matrix.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=3
  change ∃ R : (Fin 1 → Nat) → (Fin 2 → Nat) → Prop,
    PrimrecRel R ∧ ∀ xs : Fin 1 → Nat,
      (¬ xs 0 ∈ P) ↔ ∃ j : Nat, ∀ s : Nat, R xs (Fin.cons j (Fin.cons s Fin.elim0)) at hP
  obtain ⟨R, hR, hRP⟩ := hP
  let tuple (j s : Nat) : Fin 2 → Nat := Fin.cons j (Fin.cons s Fin.elim0)
  let Q (y j s : Nat) := ¬ R (fun _ => y) (tuple j s)
  -- The free tuple is constant in its coordinate. The bound tuple has
  -- coordinates j and s, tested by equality of the index with 0.
  have hUnary : Primrec fun t : Nat × Nat × Nat => (fun _ : Fin 1 => t.1) := by
    apply Primrec.fin_curry.mpr
    exact Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.fst
  have hBinary : Primrec fun t : Nat × Nat × Nat => tuple t.2.1 t.2.2 := by
    apply Primrec.fin_curry.mpr
    have hFirst : Primrec fun t : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Fin 2 => t.1.2.1 :=
      Primrec.fst.comp (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.fst)
    have hSecond : Primrec fun t : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Fin 2 => t.1.2.2 :=
      Primrec.snd.comp (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.fst)
    have hCoord : Primrec fun t : (Nat × Nat × Nat) × Fin 2 =>
        if t.2 = 0 then t.1.2.1 else t.1.2.2 :=
      Primrec.ite (Primrec.eq.comp Primrec.snd (Primrec.const 0)) hFirst hSecond
    exact hCoord.of_eq fun ⟨t, i⟩ => by fin_cases i <;> simp [tuple]
  have hQ : ComputablePred (fun t : Nat × Nat × Nat => Q t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2) :=
    (hR.comp hUnary hBinary).computablePred.not
  have hPiff (y : Nat) : y ∈ P ↔ ∀ j : Nat, ∃ s : Nat, Q y j s := by
    simpa only [Q, tuple, not_not, not_exists, not_forall] using
      not_congr (hRP (fun _ => y))
  refine ⟨Q, hQ, hPiff, ?_⟩
  dsimp only
  let H (k : Nat) : Set Nat := {y | ∀ j < k, ∃ s, Q y j s}
  let G : Set Nat := {z | z.unpair.2 ∈ H z.unpair.1}
  let B (z b : Nat) : Prop := ∀ j < z.unpair.1, ∃ s < b, Q z.unpair.2 j s
  -- The source leaves uniformity implicit. A common strict bound suffices
  -- for finitely many witnesses. At k = 0 the bound can be 0.
  have bounded (y k : Nat) (h : y ∈ H k) :
      ∃ b : Nat, ∀ j < k, ∃ s < b, Q y j s := by
    induction k with
    | zero => exact ⟨0, fun j hj => (Nat.not_lt_zero j hj).elim⟩
    | succ k ih =>
      obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := ih (fun j hj => h j (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hj))
      obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := h k (Nat.lt_succ_self k)
      refine ⟨max b (s + 1), fun j hj => ?_⟩
      rcases Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq.mp hj with hj | rfl
      · obtain ⟨t, ht, hQt⟩ := hb j hj
        exact ⟨t, lt_of_lt_of_le ht (le_max_left _ _), hQt⟩
      · exact ⟨s, lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s) (le_max_right _ _), hs⟩
  -- Tau Ceti's bounded-search lemma uses a jointly computable input test.
  -- Adapt its Boolean recursion over 0 through n-1 using the pinned mathlib
  -- primitives, so the proof needs no Tau Ceti import.
  -- The bounded and unbounded search adaptations below are from
  -- TauCeti/Computability/RE.lean, rev. 91942aa9ff8cea04d0d9905b80f75c07ce2379c4.
  -- Copyright (c) 2026 The Tau Ceti contributors. Apache-2.0.
  have existsLt {α : Type} [Primcodable α] {p : α → Nat → Prop}
      (hp : ComputablePred fun x : α × Nat => p x.1 x.2) :
      ComputablePred fun x : α × Nat => ∃ n < x.2, p x.1 n := by
    have hscan : Computable fun x : α × Nat =>
        Nat.rec (motive := fun _ => Bool) false (fun n b => b || decide (p x.1 n)) x.2 :=
      Computable.nat_rec Computable.snd (Computable.const false)
        (Primrec.or.to_comp.comp (Computable.snd.comp Computable.snd)
          (hp.decide.comp (Computable.pair (Computable.fst.comp Computable.fst)
            (Computable.fst.comp Computable.snd)))).to₂
    refine Computable.computablePred (hscan.of_eq fun ⟨a, n⟩ => ?_)
    induction n with
    | zero => simp
    | succ n ih =>
      have hsplit : (∃ m < n + 1, p a m) ↔ (∃ m < n, p a m) ∨ p a n := by
        simp only [Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq, or_and_right, exists_or, exists_eq_left]
      change (Nat.rec false (fun m b => b || decide (p a m)) n ||
        decide (p a n)) = decide (∃ m < n + 1, p a m)
      rw [ih]
      simp only [hsplit, Bool.decide_or]
  have hReorder : Computable (fun t : (Nat × Nat) × Nat => (t.1.1, t.1.2, t.2)) :=
    (Computable.fst.comp Computable.fst).pair
      ((Computable.snd.comp Computable.fst).pair Computable.snd)
  have hInner : ComputablePred fun t : (Nat × Nat) × Nat =>
      ∃ s < t.2, Q t.1.1 t.1.2 s :=
    existsLt (p := fun (yj : Nat × Nat) s => Q yj.1 yj.2 s)
      (hQ.decide.comp hReorder).computablePred
  have hUnpair : Computable Nat.unpair := Primrec.unpair.to_comp
  have hInnerInput : Computable (fun t : (Nat × Nat) × Nat =>
      ((t.1.1.unpair.2, t.2), t.1.2)) :=
    ((Computable.snd.comp (hUnpair.comp (Computable.fst.comp Computable.fst))).pair
      Computable.snd).pair (Computable.snd.comp Computable.fst)
  have hFailure : ComputablePred fun t : (Nat × Nat) × Nat =>
      ¬ ∃ s < t.1.2, Q t.1.1.unpair.2 t.2 s :=
    ((hInner.decide.comp hInnerInput).computablePred :
      ComputablePred fun t : (Nat × Nat) × Nat => ∃ s < t.1.2, Q t.1.1.unpair.2 t.2 s).not
  have hOuter := existsLt (p := fun (zb : Nat × Nat) j =>
    ¬ ∃ s < zb.2, Q zb.1.unpair.2 j s) hFailure
  have hOuterInput : Computable (fun t : Nat × Nat => (t, t.1.unpair.1)) :=
    Computable.id.pair (Computable.fst.comp (hUnpair.comp Computable.fst))
  have hB : ComputablePred (fun t : Nat × Nat => B t.1 t.2) := by
    have h := (hOuter.not.decide.comp hOuterInput).computablePred
    exact h.of_eq fun t => by simp [B]
  -- Adapt Tau Ceti's existential semidecision proof. The stage test is
  -- total, so all earlier searches satisfy the rfind domain condition.
  have hSearch : Partrec fun z => Nat.rfind fun b => Part.some (decide (B z b)) :=
    Partrec.rfind hB.decide.partrec
  have hRE : REPred (fun z => z ∈ G) := hSearch.dom_re.of_eq fun z => by
    have hDom : (Nat.rfind fun b => Part.some (decide (B z b))).Dom ↔ ∃ b, B z b := by
      simpa using Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun b => Part.some (decide (B z b)))
    rw [hDom]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨b, hb⟩ j hj
      obtain ⟨s, _, hs⟩ := hb j hj
      exact ⟨s, hs⟩
    · exact bounded z.unpair.2 z.unpair.1
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable, Steps 1.2, 2.1, 3.1.
  -- Use the compiled Nat bridge for the recognizability-to-range direction.
  -- Its fallback enumerator covers the nonempty case and uses Nat.unpair
  -- for candidate/fuel and the reviewed false-bit encoding for Nat outputs.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable
  -- The article-specific Research Portal and defect-report routes return
  -- HTTP 404. The article's claim is proved as stated on p. 3.
  refine ⟨(ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff false G).mp hRE, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · ext y
    simp
  · intro k l hkl y hy j hj
    exact hy j (lt_of_lt_of_le hj hkl)
  · -- The row k = j + 1 supplies the witness at each specified index j.
    ext y
    rw [Set.mem_iInter, hPiff]
    exact ⟨fun h k j _ => h j, fun h j => h (j + 1) j (Nat.lt_succ_self j)⟩

by
  intro A V cyl encode decode ce hnotCyl hA hAc hV hhom Z hZ
  -- Lemma 2 assumes both colours are non-c.e. The auxiliary result applies
  -- that assumption only to the colour of a marker that is actually present.

FiniteMarkerAvoidance.support:
/-- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §3, Lemma 2, pp. 4–6.
Only the colour classes represented among the finite markers need be non-c.e. -/
theorem FiniteMarkerAvoidance.of_nonCE_marker_colors
    (A : Set ℕ) (V : ℕ → Set ℕ) :
    let cyl : Set ℕ := {z | ∃ x n : ℕ, x ∈ A ∧ z = Nat.pair x n}
    let encode : ℕ → List Bool := fun n => List.replicate n true
    let decode : List Bool → Option ℕ := fun w =>
      if encode w.length = w then some w.length else none
    let ce : Set ℕ → Prop :=
      ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode
        (Function.LeftInverse.injective
          (show Function.LeftInverse List.length encode from fun _ => List.length_replicate))
        (by intro n; simp [decode, encode])
        (fun w hw => ite_eq_right (fun h => hw ⟨w.length, h⟩))
    ¬ (OneOneReducible (fun x => x ∈ A) (fun x => x ∈ cyl) ∧
        OneOneReducible (fun x => x ∈ cyl) (fun x => x ∈ A)) →
    ce {z | ∃ x y : ℕ, y ∈ V x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y} →
    (∀ x y : ℕ, y ∈ V x → (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A)) →
    ∀ Z : Set ℕ, Z.Finite →
      (∀ z ∈ Z, (z ∈ A → ¬ ce A) ∧ (z ∉ A → ¬ ce (Aᶜ))) →
      ∃ x : ℕ, (V x).Finite ∧ V x ∩ Z = ∅ := by
  classical
  intro cyl encode decode ce hnotCyl hV hhom Z hZ hcolors
  by_contra hno
  have hinfinite (x : ℕ) (havoid : V x ∩ Z = ∅) : (V x).Infinite :=
    fun hfin => hno ⟨x, hfin, havoid⟩
  have hforward : OneOneReducible (fun x => x ∈ A) (fun x => x ∈ cyl) := by
    refine ⟨fun x => Nat.pair x 0,
      Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp Computable.id (Computable.const 0), ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro x y h
      exact (Nat.pair_eq_pair.mp h).1
    · intro x
      constructor
      · intro hx
        exact ⟨x, 0, hx, rfl⟩
      · rintro ⟨y, n, hy, hp⟩
        exact (Nat.pair_eq_pair.mp hp).1.symm ▸ hy

  -- Lemma 2, pp. 4–5: the reviewed supplier provides the greedy
  -- injection for the exact true-bit c.e. row graph, homogeneity and
  -- infinitude. Its search follows the freshness and termination arguments
  -- in steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 of the Alphabeta Math item
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations.
  -- The supplier searches a different row at each input and tracks all
  -- earlier outputs. Empty restraints use the original rows directly.
  by_cases hempty : Z = ∅
  · exact hnotCyl ⟨hforward, InfiniteHomogeneousRows A V hV hhom
      (fun x => hinfinite x (by simp [hempty]))⟩

  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect-report routes
  -- returned HTTP 404. For computability, use the shared item
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable.
  -- Steps 1.1 and 3.1 inspire the range-to-domain bridge below. Its
  -- identity word encoding is replaced by the supplier's true-bit unary
  -- Nat encoding. As in step 2.1, pair candidate data with bounded fuel.
  -- The local nat_rePred_iff_exists_code supplier gives a domain code.
  -- Use evaln to certify individual memberships in place of the article's
  -- simultaneous finite stage approximations.
  let graph (W : ℕ → Set ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
    {z | ∃ x y : ℕ, y ∈ W x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y}
  have hpair (W : ℕ → Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
      n ∈ graph W ↔ n.unpair.2 ∈ W n.unpair.1 := by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨x, y, hy, rfl⟩
      simpa using hy
    · intro hy
      exact ⟨n.unpair.1, n.unpair.2, hy, (Nat.pair_unpair n).symm⟩
  have hbridge (S : Set ℕ) : REPred (fun n => n ∈ S) ↔ ce S :=
    ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff true S
  obtain ⟨code, hcode⟩ :=
    (ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff_exists_code (graph V)).mp ((hbridge _).mpr hV)
  let bounded (t x y : ℕ) : Bool := (code.evaln t (Nat.pair x y)).isSome
  have hbounded {t x y : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ} (ht : Primrec t) (hx : Primrec x) (hy : Primrec y) :
      Primrec (fun p => bounded (t p) (x p) (y p)) :=
    Primrec.option_isSome.comp
      (Nat.Partrec.Code.primrec_evaln.comp
        ((ht.pair (Primrec.const code)).pair (Primrec₂.natPair.comp hx hy)))
  have hstage (x y : ℕ) : y ∈ V x ↔ ∃ t, bounded t x y := by
    have hxy : Nat.pair x y ∈ graph V ↔ y ∈ V x := by
      simpa using hpair V (Nat.pair x y)
    rw [← hxy, ← hcode, Part.dom_iff_mem]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨out, hout⟩
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete.mp hout
      exact ⟨t, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mpr ⟨out, ht⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
      obtain ⟨out, hout⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp ht
      exact ⟨out, Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln_complete.mpr ⟨t, hout⟩⟩
  -- Minimization on a total test uses the same terminating individual
  -- tests as step 1.1, now with fuel code and markers in the witness.
  have hsearch {test : ℕ × ℕ → Bool} (htest : Primrec test) :
      REPred (fun x => ∃ k, test (x, k)) := by
    have hrec : Partrec (fun x : ℕ => Nat.rfind (fun k => Part.some (test (x, k)))) :=
      Partrec.rfind htest.to_comp.partrec
    refine hrec.dom_re.of_eq fun x => ?_
    exact (Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun k => Part.some (test (x, k)))).trans (by simp)

  have listMem {α : Type} [Primcodable α] :
      PrimrecRel (fun (xs : List α) (y : α) => y ∈ xs) :=
    (PrimrecRel.exists_mem_list (R := @Eq α) Primrec.eq).of_eq (by intro xs y; simp)
  let L := hZ.toFinset.toList
  have hL (z : ℕ) : z ∈ L ↔ z ∈ Z := by simp [L]
  let Avoid (x : ℕ) : Prop := V x ∩ Z = ∅
  by_cases hgood : ∀ z ∈ Z, ∃ d, Avoid d ∧ (d ∈ A ↔ z ∈ A)
  · -- Lemma 2, pp. 5–6: hardcode one avoiding row of the same colour
    -- for each marker. Choice supplies the constants; the recognizer
    -- only reads the resulting finite table.
    have hchoose (z : ℕ) : ∃ d, z ∈ Z → Avoid d ∧ (d ∈ A ↔ z ∈ A) := by
      by_cases hz : z ∈ Z
      · obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := hgood z hz
        exact ⟨d, fun _ => hd⟩
      · exact ⟨0, fun h => (hz h).elim⟩
    choose d hd using hchoose
    let table := L.map (fun z => (z, d z))
    have htable (z r : ℕ) : (z, r) ∈ table ↔ z ∈ Z ∧ r = d z := by
      simp [table, hL, eq_comm]
    let W (x : ℕ) : Set ℕ := {u | u ∈ V x ∨ ∃ z ∈ Z, z ∈ V x ∧ u ∈ V (d z)}
    have hW : ce (graph W) := by
      apply (hbridge _).mp
      -- Direct membership searches one fuel. Added membership searches
      -- a table entry (marker, row) and two independent successful fuels.
      let test (p : ℕ × ℕ) : Bool :=
        bounded p.2 p.1.unpair.1 p.1.unpair.2 ||
          (decide (p.2.unpair.1.unpair ∈ table) &&
            bounded p.2.unpair.2.unpair.1 p.1.unpair.1 p.2.unpair.1.unpair.1 &&
            bounded p.2.unpair.2.unpair.2 p.2.unpair.1.unpair.2 p.1.unpair.2)
      have hinput := Primrec.unpair.comp (Primrec.fst : Primrec (Prod.fst : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ))
      have hwitness := Primrec.unpair.comp (Primrec.snd : Primrec (Prod.snd : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ))
      have hentry := Primrec.unpair.comp (Primrec.fst.comp hwitness)
      have hfuel := Primrec.unpair.comp (Primrec.snd.comp hwitness)
      have hrow := Primrec.fst.comp hinput
      have hvalue := Primrec.snd.comp hinput
      have htest : Primrec test :=
        Primrec.or.comp (hbounded Primrec.snd hrow hvalue)
          (Primrec.and.comp
            (Primrec.and.comp (listMem.decide.comp (Primrec.const table) hentry)
              (hbounded (Primrec.fst.comp hfuel) hrow (Primrec.fst.comp hentry)))
            (hbounded (Primrec.snd.comp hfuel) (Primrec.snd.comp hentry) hvalue))
      refine (hsearch htest).of_eq fun n => ?_
      rw [hpair]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        simp only [test, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at hk
        rcases hk with h | ⟨⟨hentry, ht₁⟩, ht₂⟩
        · exact Or.inl ((hstage _ _).mpr ⟨k, h⟩)
        · obtain ⟨hz, hr⟩ := (htable k.unpair.1.unpair.1 k.unpair.1.unpair.2).mp hentry
          exact Or.inr ⟨_, hz, (hstage _ _).mpr ⟨_, ht₁⟩,
            hr ▸ (hstage _ _).mpr ⟨_, ht₂⟩⟩
      · intro hu
        change _ ∨ _ at hu
        rcases hu with hu | ⟨z, hz, hzx, hu⟩
        · obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := (hstage _ _).mp hu
          exact ⟨t, by simp [test, ht]⟩
        · obtain ⟨t₁, ht₁⟩ := (hstage _ _).mp hzx
          obtain ⟨t₂, ht₂⟩ := (hstage _ _).mp hu
          exact ⟨Nat.pair (Nat.pair z (d z)) (Nat.pair t₁ t₂),
            by simp [test, htable, hz, ht₁, ht₂]⟩
    have hWhom (x u : ℕ) (hu : u ∈ W x) : u ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A := by
      rcases hu with hu | ⟨z, hz, hzx, hu⟩
      · exact hhom x u hu
      · exact (hhom (d z) u hu).trans ((hd z hz).2.trans (hhom x z hzx))
    have hWinf (x : ℕ) : (W x).Infinite := by
      by_cases ha : Avoid x
      · exact (hinfinite x ha).mono (fun _ hu => Or.inl hu)
      · obtain ⟨z, hzx, hz⟩ := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr ha
        exact (hinfinite (d z) (hd z hz).1).mono (fun _ hu => Or.inr ⟨z, hz, hzx, hu⟩)
    exact hnotCyl ⟨hforward, InfiniteHomogeneousRows A W hW hWhom hWinf⟩

  · -- Lemma 2, p. 6: a marker with no avoiding row of the same colour
    -- witnesses an entire colour class covered by its same-colour sections.
    obtain ⟨z, hz, hcover⟩ : ∃ z ∈ Z, ∀ x, Avoid x → ¬ (x ∈ A ↔ z ∈ A) := by
      simpa only [not_forall, not_exists, not_and, exists_prop] using hgood
    let markers := L.filter (fun w => decide (w ∈ A ↔ z ∈ A))
    have hmarkers (w : ℕ) : w ∈ markers ↔ w ∈ Z ∧ (w ∈ A ↔ z ∈ A) := by
      simp [markers, hL]
    let test (p : ℕ × ℕ) : Bool :=
      decide (p.2.unpair.1 ∈ markers) && bounded p.2.unpair.2 p.1 p.2.unpair.1
    have hwitness := Primrec.unpair.comp (Primrec.snd : Primrec (Prod.snd : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ))
    have hmarker := Primrec.fst.comp hwitness
    have htest : Primrec test :=
      Primrec.and.comp (listMem.decide.comp (Primrec.const markers) hmarker)
        (hbounded (Primrec.snd.comp hwitness) Primrec.fst hmarker)
    let color : Set ℕ := {x | x ∈ A ↔ z ∈ A}
    have hceColor : ce color := by
      apply (hbridge _).mp
      refine (hsearch htest).of_eq fun x => ?_
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        simp only [test, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at hk
        have hw := (hstage _ _).mpr ⟨_, hk.2⟩
        exact (hhom x _ hw).symm.trans ((hmarkers _).mp hk.1).2
      · intro hx
        have hhit : ¬ Avoid x := fun ha => hcover x ha hx
        obtain ⟨w, hwx, hwZ⟩ := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr hhit
        have hw := (hmarkers w).mpr ⟨hwZ, (hhom x w hwx).trans hx⟩
        obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := (hstage _ _).mp hwx
        exact ⟨Nat.pair w t, by simp [test, hw, ht]⟩
    by_cases hzA : z ∈ A
    · have hEq : color = A := Set.ext (fun x => by simp [color, hzA])
      exact (hcolors z hz).1 hzA (hEq ▸ hceColor)
    · have hEq : color = Aᶜ := Set.ext (fun x => by simp [color, hzA])
      exact (hcolors z hz).2 hzA (hEq ▸ hceColor)

ReducibilityImplications.support:
namespace ReducibilityImplications

/-- Finite-one reducibility on natural-number sets, with the article's singleton fibres. -/
abbrev FiniteOneReducible (X Y : Set Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Nat → Nat, Computable f ∧
    (∀ y : Nat, (Set.preimage f ({y} : Set Nat)).Finite) ∧
    (∀ x : Nat, x ∈ X ↔ f x ∈ Y)

theorem finiteOneRefl (X : Set Nat) : FiniteOneReducible X X := by
  -- Alphabeta Math, def-computable-many-one-reducibility-interface,
  -- verification step 1.1 gives the identity witness on Nat. Its fibres are singletons.
  exact ⟨id, Computable.id, fun y => Set.finite_singleton y, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩

theorem finiteOneTrans {X Y Z : Set Nat}
    (hXY : FiniteOneReducible X Y) (hYZ : FiniteOneReducible Y Z) :
    FiniteOneReducible X Z := by
  -- The same verification step 1.1 gives computable composition and composes
  -- the membership equivalences. The finite-one hypothesis adds a fibre check.
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfFinite, hfMem⟩ := hXY
  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgFinite, hgMem⟩ := hYZ
  refine ⟨g ∘ f, hg.comp hf, ?_, fun x => (hfMem x).trans (hgMem (f x))⟩
  intro y
  -- The composite fibre is the preimage under f of the finite g-fibre.
  -- All f-fibres over that target set are finite by hfFinite.
  change (Set.preimage f (Set.preimage g ({y} : Set Nat))).Finite
  exact (hgFinite y).preimage' (fun z _ => hfFinite z)

abbrev finiteOneDegree (X : Set Nat) : Set (Set Nat) :=
  {Y | FiniteOneReducible Y X ∧ FiniteOneReducible X Y}

theorem finiteOneDegree_eq_iff {X Y : Set Nat} :
    finiteOneDegree X = finiteOneDegree Y ↔
      FiniteOneReducible X Y ∧ FiniteOneReducible Y X := by
  -- Cintioli, §2, pp. 2–3: equal classes contain X in common by
  -- reflexivity. Mutual reductions transport every class member by transitivity.
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hXX : X ∈ finiteOneDegree X := ⟨finiteOneRefl X, finiteOneRefl X⟩
    rw [h] at hXX
    exact hXX
  · rintro ⟨hXY, hYX⟩
    ext Z
    change (FiniteOneReducible Z X ∧ FiniteOneReducible X Z) ↔
      (FiniteOneReducible Z Y ∧ FiniteOneReducible Y Z)
    exact ⟨fun ⟨hZX, hXZ⟩ => ⟨finiteOneTrans hZX hXY, finiteOneTrans hYX hXZ⟩,
      fun ⟨hZY, hYZ⟩ => ⟨finiteOneTrans hZY hYX, finiteOneTrans hXY hYZ⟩⟩

end ReducibilityImplications
