CofiniteDomainLemma.proof:
by
  intro A φ cyl hnonrec hnoncyl hφ hasc
  classical
  -- Cintioli, §3, Definition 3 and Lemma 4, pp. 6–7.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=6
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect report returned
  -- HTTP 404. The proof follows the v1 source and the compiled row supplier.
  by_contra hfinite
  let F : Set ℕ := {x : ℕ | (φ x).Dom}ᶜ
  have hF : F.Finite := not_not.mp hfinite

  -- Finite lists of constants give computable membership tests. Thus a
  -- finite colour, or its computable complement, would make A recursive.
  have hmemRelation : PrimrecRel (fun (xs : List ℕ) (x : ℕ) => x ∈ xs) :=
    (PrimrecRel.exists_mem_list (R := @Eq ℕ) Primrec.eq).of_eq (by
      intro xs x
      simp)
  have hlistMem (xs : List ℕ) : ComputablePred (fun x : ℕ => x ∈ xs) :=
    (hmemRelation.decide.to_comp.comp (Computable.const xs) Computable.id).computablePred
  have hfiniteComp (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S.Finite) : ComputablePred (fun x : ℕ => x ∈ S) :=
    (hlistMem hS.toFinset.toList).of_eq fun x =>
      Finset.mem_toList.trans hS.mem_toFinset
  have hA : A.Infinite := fun h => hnonrec (hfiniteComp A h)
  have hAc : Aᶜ.Infinite := fun h =>
    hnonrec ((hfiniteComp Aᶜ h).not.of_eq (fun x => by simp))

  have htarget (x : ℕ) : ∃ y : ℕ, x < y ∧ (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A) := by
    by_cases hx : x ∈ A
    · obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hA.exists_gt x
      exact ⟨y, hxy, iff_of_true hy hx⟩
    · obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hAc.exists_gt x
      exact ⟨y, hxy, iff_of_false hy hx⟩
  choose target htarget_spec using htarget
  let exceptions := hF.toFinset.toList
  have hexceptions (x : ℕ) : x ∈ exceptions ↔ ¬ (φ x).Dom :=
    Finset.mem_toList.trans hF.mem_toFinset

  -- Lemma 4 hardcodes the chosen values only on the finite exceptional set.
  -- The induction implements this table by equality tests and constants.
  have hlookup (xs : List ℕ) :
      Computable (fun x : ℕ => if x ∈ xs then target x else 0) := by
    induction xs with
    | nil => simpa using (Computable.const (0 : ℕ) : Computable (fun _ : ℕ => 0))
    | cons a xs ih =>
      have heq : ComputablePred (fun x : ℕ => x = a) :=
        (Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp Computable.id (Computable.const a)).computablePred
      refine (ComputablePred.ite (Computable.const (target a)) ih heq).of_eq ?_
      intro x
      by_cases hx : x = a
      · subst x
        simp
      · simp [hx]
  let patch (x : ℕ) : Part ℕ :=
    if x ∈ exceptions then Part.some (target x) else φ x
  have hpatch : Partrec patch := by
    refine (Partrec.cond (hlistMem exceptions).decide
      (hlookup exceptions).partrec hφ).of_eq ?_
    intro x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ exceptions <;> simp [patch, hx]
  have hdom (x : ℕ) : (patch x).Dom := by
    by_cases hx : x ∈ exceptions
    · simp [patch, hx]
    · simpa only [patch, ite_eq_right hx] using not_not.mp (mt (hexceptions x).mpr hx)
  let g (x : ℕ) := (patch x).get (hdom x)
  have hgmem (x : ℕ) : g x ∈ patch x := Part.get_mem (hdom x)
  have hg : Computable g := hpatch.of_eq_tot hgmem
  have hg_spec (x : ℕ) : x < g x ∧ (g x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A) := by
    by_cases hx : x ∈ exceptions
    · have h : g x = target x := by simpa [patch, hx] using hgmem x
      rw [h]
      exact htarget_spec x
    · exact hasc x (g x) (by simpa only [patch, ite_eq_right hx] using hgmem x)

  let orbit (x n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.rec x (fun _ y => g y) n
  let W (x : ℕ) := Set.range (orbit x)
  have horbit : Computable₂ orbit :=
    (Computable.nat_rec Computable.snd Computable.fst (hg.comp
      (Computable.snd.comp Computable.snd)).to₂).to₂
  have hinfinite (x : ℕ) : (W x).Infinite :=
    Set.infinite_range_of_injective (strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ (f := orbit x)
      (fun n => (hg_spec (orbit x n)).1)).injective
  have hcolour (x n : ℕ) : orbit x n ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A := by
    induction n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ n ih => exact (hg_spec (orbit x n)).2.trans ih
  have hhom (x y : ℕ) (hy : y ∈ W x) : y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A := by
    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hy
    exact hcolour x n

  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable
  -- Step 1.1 searches a total enumerator. Here the values being enumerated
  -- are packed Nat pairs.
  -- The compiled ComputablyEnumerableSet range recognizer and true-bit
  -- bridge supply the c.e. graph premise with the supplier’s encoding.
  -- Both apply to Nat sets, so the optional Tau Ceti import is unnecessary.
  let graph : Set ℕ := {z | ∃ x y : ℕ, y ∈ W x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y}
  let pack (i : ℕ) := Nat.pair i.unpair.1 (orbit i.unpair.1 i.unpair.2)
  have hpack : Computable pack :=
    (Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp Computable.fst horbit).comp Computable.unpair
  have hgraph : Set.range pack = graph := by
    ext z
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨i.unpair.1, orbit i.unpair.1 i.unpair.2, ⟨i.unpair.2, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨x, y, ⟨n, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨Nat.pair x n, by simp [pack, Nat.unpair_pair]⟩
  have hRE : REPred (fun z => z ∈ graph) := by
    rw [← hgraph]
    exact ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_range hpack

  -- Lemma 4 builds its fresh-output reduction directly. We apply the
  -- reviewed §3 observation to these orbit rows.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations
  -- Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 motivate keeping prior outputs, freshness and
  -- termination. The supplier uses the row indexed by each input; it
  -- therefore needs uniform enumerability and infinitude for every row.
  have hbackward : OneOneReducible (fun z => z ∈ cyl) (fun x => x ∈ A) :=
    InfiniteHomogeneousRows A W
      ((ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff true graph).mp hRE) hhom hinfinite
  have hforward : OneOneReducible (fun x => x ∈ A) (fun z => z ∈ cyl) := by
    refine ⟨fun x => Nat.pair x 0,
      Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp Computable.id (Computable.const 0), ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro x y h
      exact congrArg Prod.fst (Nat.pairEquiv.injective h : (x, 0) = (y, 0))
    · intro x
      change x ∈ A ↔ ∃ y n : ℕ, y ∈ A ∧ Nat.pair x 0 = Nat.pair y n
      constructor
      · exact fun hx => ⟨x, 0, hx, rfl⟩
      · rintro ⟨y, n, hy, heq⟩
        have hxy : x = y :=
          congrArg Prod.fst (Nat.pairEquiv.injective heq : (x, 0) = (y, n))
        exact hxy ▸ hy
  exact hnoncyl ⟨hforward, hbackward⟩
CofiniteDomainLemma.support:
/-- Race two partial computable maps. The domain is their union, and every
    returned value is an output of one of the two maps at the same input. -/
theorem CofiniteDomainLemma.partrec_union
    {φ ψ : ℕ → Part ℕ} (hφ : Partrec φ) (hψ : Partrec ψ) :
    ∃ χ : ℕ → Part ℕ, Partrec χ ∧
      (∀ x, (χ x).Dom ↔ (φ x).Dom ∨ (ψ x).Dom) ∧
      (∀ x y, y ∈ χ x → y ∈ φ x ∨ y ∈ ψ x) := by
  -- For the c.e. branch, the coordinator asks for the bounded-code race.
  -- Nat.Partrec.merge' already implements it: at each fuel, try both codes
  -- with left priority at equal fuel, then use rfindOpt for the first success.
  -- Its soundness and completeness give both clauses even when the maps
  -- return different values on their common domain.
  obtain ⟨χ, hχ, hspec⟩ :=
    Nat.Partrec.merge' (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hφ) (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hψ)
  exact ⟨χ, Partrec.nat_iff.mpr hχ, fun x => (hspec x).2,
    fun x => (hspec x).1⟩

external.usage: In Nat, each infinite colour class has a member strictly above a given exceptional input.
If the complement of A were finite, its computable membership test would give a computable membership test for A by negation.
Use computable membership in the finite exceptional list to choose the total lookup branch or the original partial map.
Compute each orbit from its initial point by recursion on the iteration count, using the total computable patched map at each step.
Computably pack the orbit graph into Nat and construct the forward reduction by pairing with zero.
Use injectivity of the equivalence to prove injectivity of the forward reduction and recover the first coordinate for membership reflection.
Specialize to equality of naturals and hold the finite list constant to obtain computable membership for finite colour classes and for the exception list.
Use the supplied domain proof at each input to obtain a member of the patched partial computation, then conclude that the resulting total map is computable.

Implement CofiniteDomainLemma.partrec_union by racing two bounded code evaluations in increasing fuel with left priority at ties. The theorem gives the union of their domains and certifies that each output comes from either input computation.

FixedStageRowStability.proof:
by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §4, p. 8, upper strategy:
  -- failure of stability at t is witnessed by a later stage with a different row.
  -- Monotonicity identifies such a change with a new entry. The stability test
  -- itself needs only computable stage codes, independently of row exhaustion.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=8
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math collection and defect report returned
  -- HTTP 404. The numbered steps below refer to the shared-library proof.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete
  intro φ hφ stage hstage _hmonotone _V _hexhaustion
  classical
  -- Step 1.2 searches a total witness test. Here stage-code computability
  -- supplies the test directly, so a primitive-recursive matrix is unnecessary.
  -- The offset d ensures that every tested stage is at least t.
  let stageInput (p : Nat × Nat) : Nat × Nat × Nat :=
    (p.1.unpair.1, p.1.unpair.2.unpair.1, p.1.unpair.2.unpair.2 + p.2)
  let stageCode (n d : Nat) : Nat :=
    let q := stageInput (n, d)
    Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (stage q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2)
  have hcode : Computable₂ stageCode := by
    have houter : Computable (fun p : Nat × Nat => p.1.unpair) :=
      Computable.unpair.comp Computable.fst
    have hinner : Computable (fun p : Nat × Nat => p.1.unpair.2.unpair) :=
      Computable.unpair.comp (Computable.snd.comp houter)
    have hoffset : Computable (fun p : Nat × Nat => p.1.unpair.2.unpair.2 + p.2) :=
      Primrec.nat_add.to_comp.comp (Computable.snd.comp hinner) Computable.snd
    have hinput : Computable stageInput :=
      (Computable.fst.comp houter).pair ((Computable.fst.comp hinner).pair hoffset)
    exact hstage.comp hinput
  let changed (n d : Nat) : Prop := stageCode n d ≠ stageCode n 0
  have hbaseline : Computable (fun p : Nat × Nat => stageCode p.1 0) :=
    hcode.comp Computable.fst (Computable.const 0)
  have hchanged : ComputablePred (fun p : Nat × Nat => changed p.1 p.2) :=
    ((Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp hcode hbaseline).computablePred).not
  -- Adapt TauCeti's ComputablePred.rePred_exists. Retain the partial
  -- function itself for indexing, and use totality to discharge the
  -- smaller-input domain premises of Nat.rfind_dom.
  let search (n : Nat) := Nat.rfind (fun d => Part.some (decide (changed n d)))
  have hsearch : Partrec search := Partrec.rfind hchanged.decide.partrec
  have hdomain (n : Nat) : (search n).Dom ↔ ∃ d : Nat, changed n d := by
    simpa [search] using
      (Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun d => Part.some (decide (changed n d))))
  -- Step 2.1 hard-wires the parameter into the index and queries at 0.
  -- Surjectivity of the reviewed numbering gives one fixed search index i.
  -- Carry the packed triple as its input, so the query map is n ↦ ⟨i, n⟩.
  -- This proves the needed halting reduction directly. The compiled tape
  -- decision theorem implements the negative answer in the reviewed model.
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hφ.2.1 search hsearch
  intro K
  have hquery := OracleNegativePullbackDecision K (Nat.pair i)
    (Primrec₂.natPair.comp (Primrec.const i) Primrec.id).to_comp
  convert hquery using 1
  ext n
  change (∀ r : Nat, n.unpair.2.unpair.2 ≤ r →
    stage n.unpair.1 n.unpair.2.unpair.1 r =
      stage n.unpair.1 n.unpair.2.unpair.1 n.unpair.2.unpair.2) ↔
    ¬ (φ (Nat.pair i n).unpair.1 (Nat.pair i n).unpair.2).Dom
  rw [Nat.unpair_pair]
  change _ ↔ ¬ (φ i n).Dom
  rw [hi, hdomain, not_exists]
  -- The binary code is injective. Recover every r ≥ t with d = r - t.
  simp only [changed, not_not, stageCode, stageInput, Nat.add_zero, EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h d
    exact h _ (Nat.le_add_right _ _)
  · intro h r hr
    simpa [Nat.add_sub_of_le hr] using h (r - n.unpair.2.unpair.2)

external.usage: Adapted the unbounded-witness search in ComputablePred.rePred_exists. Apply Partrec.rfind to the total stage-change test and use Nat.rfind_dom to show that the search terminates exactly when some later stage differs. Retain the natural-valued partial function so AcceptableNumbering supplies a single index.

ComputableInjectiveSection.proof:
by
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect report return HTTP 404.
  -- There is no verified numbered proof to cite. We follow the unnumbered
  -- proof of Lemma 1 on p. 4 of arXiv:2609.00419v1.
  intro p hp hsurj
  -- For each target y, surjectivity supplies a witness to p n = y.
  have hpreimage : ∀ y : Nat, ∃ n : Nat, p n = y := hsurj
  let s (y : Nat) : Nat := Nat.find (hpreimage y)
  -- Computable.find formalizes the article's μ-search. Its test is
  -- computable by composing Nat equality with p and the pair projections.
  have htest : ComputablePred (fun q : Nat × Nat => p q.2 = q.1) :=
    (Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp (hp.comp Computable.snd) Computable.fst).computablePred
  have hs : Computable s :=
    Computable.find (P := fun y n => p n = y) htest hpreimage
  have hsection (y : Nat) : p (s y) = y := Nat.find_spec (hpreimage y)
  refine ⟨s, hs, ?_, hsection, ?_⟩
  · intro y z hyz
    exact (hsection y).symm.trans ((congrArg p hyz).trans (hsection z))
  · -- The translation makes the least-witness convention of μ explicit.
    intro y n hn
    exact Nat.find_min' (hpreimage y) hn

external.usage: Applied to the decidable relation P(y,n) := p(n) = y on Nat × Nat. The computable equality test uses the given computable p, and surjectivity gives a witness for each y. The supplier proves computability of the least-preimage function defined with Nat.find.

CylinderGreatestFiniteOneDegree.proof:
by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §1, p. 1 and §2, pp. 2–3.
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math Research Portal and defect report
  -- both returned HTTP 404 on recheck.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
  -- Use verification step 1.1 of the shared-library item
  -- def-computable-many-one-reducibility-interface for composition of total
  -- Nat witnesses and their membership equivalences. Step 2.1 concerns
  -- canonical binary strings; the endpoint uses only Nat representatives.
  intro A cyl finiteOneReducible
  -- The pairing identities characterize membership via the first projection.
  have mem_cyl (z : Nat) : z ∈ cyl ↔ (Nat.unpair z).1 ∈ A := by
    change (∃ x n : Nat, x ∈ A ∧ z = Nat.pair x n) ↔ _
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨x, n, hx, rfl⟩
      simpa only [Nat.unpair_pair] using hx
    · intro hz
      exact ⟨(Nat.unpair z).1, (Nat.unpair z).2, hz, (Nat.pair_unpair z).symm⟩
  have mem_pair (x n : Nat) : Nat.pair x n ∈ cyl ↔ x ∈ A := by
    simpa only [Nat.unpair_pair] using mem_cyl (Nat.pair x n)
  -- The article's projection and zero-column maps give mutual many-one
  -- reducibility. Mathlib expresses their equivalence as equality of degrees.
  refine ⟨ManyOneDegree.of_eq_of.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨fun z => (Nat.unpair z).1,
      Computable.fst.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp, mem_cyl⟩
  · exact ⟨fun x => Nat.pair x 0,
      Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp Computable.id (Computable.const 0),
      fun x => (mem_pair x 0).symm⟩
  · intro B hDegree
    obtain ⟨f, hf, hfMem⟩ := (ManyOneDegree.of_eq_of.mp hDegree).1
    -- The second coordinate preserves the input, even when f has infinite fibres.
    have hOne : OneOneReducible (fun x : Nat => x ∈ B) (fun z : Nat => z ∈ cyl) := by
      refine ⟨fun x => Nat.pair (f x) x,
        Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp hf Computable.id, ?_,
        fun x => (hfMem x).trans (mem_pair (f x) x).symm⟩
      intro x y h
      have hPair : Nat.pairEquiv (f x, x) = Nat.pairEquiv (f y, y) := h
      exact congrArg Prod.snd (Nat.pairEquiv.injective hPair)
    -- The reviewed endpoint compares representatives as in §2, p. 3.
    -- ReducibilityImplications supplies the finite fibres from injectivity.
    exact (ReducibilityImplications B cyl).1 hOne

external.usage: Use Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp to combine the identity and zero maps, and to combine the many-one witness from B to A with the identity.
Compose the computable first projection with Primrec.unpair.to_comp to reduce the cylinder to A.
Use Nat.unpair_pair and Nat.pair_unpair for cylinder membership and Nat.pairEquiv.injective to recover the input from the second coordinate of the reduction witness.
Use mutual many-one reductions on Nat to prove equality of the cylinder and A degrees, and extract the reduction from B to A from the assumed equality of degrees.

InfiniteCEInjectiveEnumeration.proof:
by
  intro α encode decode hInjective hDecode hInvalid A hce hA
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, Lemma 1, p. 4, uses the Nat instance
  -- to enumerate R without repetitions. The article-specific Alphabeta Math
  -- Research Portal and its defect report both returned HTTP 404.
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations,
  -- step 1.1: unfold the reviewed c.e. supplier and discard its empty case.
  -- Store the binary outputs of e, as suggested by the step's codeword scan.
  -- The reviewed supplier makes these outputs computable on List Bool, so no
  -- computability assumption on decode or Primcodable instance on α is needed.
  rcases hce with hEmpty | ⟨e, he, heRange⟩
  · subst A
    exact (hA Set.finite_empty).elim
  let code (n : ℕ) := encode (e n)
  have hcode : Computable code := he
  have hcodeRange : Set.range code = encode '' A := by
    simpa only [code, Function.comp_def, heRange] using (Set.range_comp encode e)
  have hcodeInfinite : (Set.range code).Infinite := by
    rw [hcodeRange]
    exact hA.image hInjective.injOn

  -- Steps 1.1 and 3.1: search from the start for the least input whose
  -- codeword is absent from the history. Prove termination at this point,
  -- since each finite history omits a value of the infinite codeword range.
  -- The least-fresh search and list recursion follow the construction behind
  -- Tau Ceti's Computable.exists_injective_range (91942aa9ff8cea04d0d9905b80f75c07ce2379c4),
  -- specialized to Nat input and binary outputs and proved with pinned mathlib.
  let fresh (seen : List (List Bool)) (n : ℕ) : Prop := code n ∉ seen
  let decidableFresh : DecidableRel fresh := fun seen n =>
    inferInstanceAs (Decidable (code n ∉ seen))
  have hfreshExists (seen : List (List Bool)) : ∃ n, fresh seen n := by
    obtain ⟨_, ⟨n, rfl⟩, hn⟩ := hcodeInfinite.exists_notMem_finite seen.finite_toSet
    exact ⟨n, hn⟩
  have hmem : PrimrecRel (fun (seen : List (List Bool)) (w : List Bool) => w ∈ seen) :=
    (PrimrecRel.exists_mem_list (R := @Eq (List Bool)) Primrec.eq).of_eq
      (by intro seen w; simp)
  have htest : ComputablePred (fun p : List (List Bool) × ℕ => fresh p.1 p.2) :=
    (hmem.not.decide.to_comp.comp Computable.fst (hcode.comp Computable.snd)).computablePred
  let next (seen : List (List Bool)) : ℕ := @Nat.find (fresh seen) (decidableFresh seen) (hfreshExists seen)
  have hnext : Computable next := @Computable.find _ _ fresh decidableFresh htest hfreshExists
  let history (n : ℕ) : List (List Bool) :=
    Nat.rec [] (fun _ seen => code (next seen) :: seen) n
  have hstep : Computable₂
      (fun (_ : ℕ) (p : ℕ × List (List Bool)) => code (next p.2) :: p.2) :=
    (Computable.list_cons.comp (hcode.comp (hnext.comp (Computable.snd.comp Computable.snd)))
      (Computable.snd.comp Computable.snd)).to₂
  have hhistory : Computable history :=
    Computable.nat_rec Computable.id (Computable.const ([] : List (List Bool))) hstep
  let index (n : ℕ) := next (history n)
  let f (n : ℕ) := e (index n)
  have hf : Computable (fun n => encode (f n)) := hcode.comp (hnext.comp hhistory)

  -- Step 2.1: the history at stage n contains exactly the earlier outputs,
  -- and the selected output at stage n is fresh.
  have hh (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
      w ∈ history n ↔ ∃ i < n, code (index i) = w := by
    induction n with
    | zero => simp [history]
    | succ n ih =>
      change w ∈ code (index n) :: history n ↔ _
      rw [List.mem_cons, ih]
      constructor
      · rintro (rfl | ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩)
        · exact ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n, rfl⟩
        · exact ⟨i, Nat.lt_trans hi (Nat.lt_succ_self n), rfl⟩
      · rintro ⟨i, hi, heq⟩
        rcases lt_or_eq_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt_succ hi) with hlt | rfl
        · exact Or.inr ⟨i, hlt, heq⟩
        · exact Or.inl heq.symm
  have hfresh (n : ℕ) : code (index n) ∉ history n :=
    @Nat.find_spec (fresh (history n)) (decidableFresh (history n)) (hfreshExists (history n))
  have hne (i j : ℕ) (hij : i < j) : f i ≠ f j := by
    intro heq
    exact hfresh j ((hh j _).mpr ⟨i, hij, congrArg encode heq⟩)
  have hinjective : Function.Injective f := by
    intro i j heq
    rcases lt_trichotomy i j with hij | hij | hji
    · exact (hne i j hij heq).elim
    · exact hij
    · exact (hne j i hji heq.symm).elim

  -- Step 2.1, coverage: any input below the least fresh index has already
  -- appeared. The history at the next stage also contains the current output.
  -- Thus the chosen indices grow strictly and eventually pass each input.
  have hbelow (n k : ℕ) (hk : k < index n) : code k ∈ history n :=
    not_not.mp (@Nat.find_min (fresh (history n)) (decidableFresh (history n))
      (hfreshExists (history n)) k hk)
  have hthrough (n k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ index n) : code k ∈ history (n + 1) := by
    change code k ∈ code (index n) :: history n
    rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hk with hlt | heq
    · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (hbelow n k hlt)
    · rw [heq]
      exact List.mem_cons_self
  have hindex (n : ℕ) : n ≤ index n := by
    induction n with
    | zero => exact Nat.zero_le _
    | succ n ih =>
      have hlt : index n < index (n + 1) := by
        apply lt_of_not_ge
        intro hn
        exact hfresh (n + 1) (hthrough n (index (n + 1)) hn)
      exact Nat.succ_le_of_lt (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt ih hlt)

  -- Step 4.1: lift codeword coverage to A using injectivity of encode.
  refine ⟨f, hf, hinjective, ?_⟩
  rw [← heRange]
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · rintro _ ⟨n, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨index n, rfl⟩
  · rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩
    have hk : k < index (k + 1) := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self k) (hindex (k + 1))
    obtain ⟨i, _, hi⟩ := (hh (k + 1) (code k)).mp (hbelow (k + 1) k hk)
    exact ⟨i, hInjective hi⟩

external.usage: Direct. The computable decidable test checks whether the binary output at an input index is absent from the seen list. The infinite codeword range supplies a witness for every seen list.
Direct. Recurses from the empty list of binary words and prepends the output at the least fresh input index. The nested list carrier is Primcodable.
Direct. Specializes the relation to equality of List Bool to compute membership in a finite history of binary words.

Adapts the proof of the Nat-input case to List Bool outputs using the pinned mathlib. The construction retains the chosen input index to recover the original value from the supplied enumerator. The coverage argument uses strict increase of the chosen indices. No Tau Ceti import is required.

ProfileRealization.proof:
by
  classical
  intro P hP
  -- Cintioli, Lemma 1, §2, pp. 3–4, constructs a descending sequence and
  -- adds an unconditional level 0 to its packed graph.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=3
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and its defect report both
  -- returned HTTP 404.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
  -- The article proof is unnumbered. The verified library
  -- steps for the injective enumeration are cited at their application below.
  obtain ⟨Q, _, _, hG, hH0, hAnti, hPinter⟩ :=
    PiTwoDescendingCePresentation P hP
  let H (k : Nat) : Set Nat := {y | ∀ j < k, ∃ s, Q y j s}
  let G : Set Nat := {z | z.unpair.2 ∈ H z.unpair.1}
  let encode (n : Nat) : List Bool := List.replicate n false
  let decode (w : List Bool) : Option Nat :=
    if w = encode w.length then some w.length else none
  have hEncode : Function.Injective encode := List.replicate_left_injective false
  have hDecode (n : Nat) : decode (encode n) = some n := by
    simp [decode, encode]
  have hInvalid (w : List Bool) (hw : w ∉ Set.range encode) : decode w = none :=
    ite_eq_right (fun h => hw ⟨w.length, h.symm⟩)
  change ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode hEncode hDecode hInvalid G at hG
  change H 0 = Set.univ at hH0
  change Antitone H at hAnti
  change P = ⋂ k, H k at hPinter
  have hGre : REPred (fun z => z ∈ G) :=
    (ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff false G).mpr hG

  -- The article leaves the c.e. recombination implicit. A single
  -- computable preimage implements it. Both input levels 0 and 1
  -- map to level 0 of G, which contains every second coordinate.
  let shift (z : Nat) : Nat := Nat.pair z.unpair.1.pred z.unpair.2
  let R : Set Nat := {z | shift z ∈ G}
  have hFirst : Computable (fun z : Nat => z.unpair.1) :=
    Computable.fst.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp
  have hSecond : Computable (fun z : Nat => z.unpair.2) :=
    Computable.snd.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp
  have hShift : Computable shift :=
    Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp (Primrec.pred.to_comp.comp hFirst) hSecond
  have hRre : REPred (fun z => z ∈ R) := by
    change Partrec (fun z : Nat => Part.assert (z ∈ G) (fun _ => Part.some ())) at hGre
    exact hGre.comp hShift
  have hRce : ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode hEncode hDecode hInvalid R :=
    (ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff false R).mp hRre
  have hRzero (y : Nat) : Nat.pair 0 y ∈ R := by
    simp [R, shift, G, Nat.unpair_pair, hH0]
  have hRsucc (k y : Nat) : Nat.pair (k + 1) y ∈ R ↔ y ∈ H k := by
    simp [R, shift, G, Nat.unpair_pair]
  have hPairRight (k : Nat) : Function.Injective (Nat.pair k) := by
    intro y z hyz
    exact congrArg Prod.snd (Nat.pairEquiv.injective (show
      Nat.pairEquiv (k, y) = Nat.pairEquiv (k, z) from hyz))
  have hPairLeft (y : Nat) : Function.Injective (fun k => Nat.pair k y) := by
    intro j k hjk
    exact congrArg Prod.fst (Nat.pairEquiv.injective (show
      Nat.pairEquiv (j, y) = Nat.pairEquiv (k, y) from hjk))
  have hRinf : R.Infinite :=
    (Set.infinite_range_of_injective (hPairRight 0)).mono (by
      rintro _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
      exact hRzero y)

  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations,
  -- steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1, scans distinct codewords, proves exact coverage,
  -- and uses infinitude for termination. The compiled supplier encapsulates
  -- these steps. Its computability conclusion is for the encoded outputs.
  -- Recover computability of r by taking the length of each false-bit codeword.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations
  obtain ⟨r, hrCode, hrInj, hrRange⟩ :=
    InfiniteCEInjectiveEnumeration encode decode hEncode hDecode hInvalid R hRce hRinf
  have hr : Computable r :=
    (Computable.list_length.comp hrCode).of_eq (fun n => List.length_replicate)
  let p (n : Nat) : Nat := (r n).unpair.2
  have hp : Computable p := hSecond.comp hr
  have hpSurj : Function.Surjective p := by
    intro y
    have h := hRzero y
    rw [← hrRange] at h
    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := h
    exact ⟨n, by simp [p, hn, Nat.unpair_pair]⟩
  refine ⟨p, hp, hpSurj, ?_, ?_⟩
  · ext y
    -- The article counts fibres. Use the exact image under r to transport
    -- infinitude to the packed column and use a finite bound on its levels.
    let C : Set Nat := {z | z ∈ R ∧ z.unpair.2 = y}
    have hImage : r '' (p ⁻¹' ({y} : Set Nat)) = C := by
      ext z
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩
        change r n ∈ R ∧ p n = y
        exact ⟨hrRange ▸ Set.mem_range_self n, Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hn⟩
      · rintro ⟨hzR, hzy⟩
        rw [← hrRange] at hzR
        obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hzR
        exact ⟨n, Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr hzy, rfl⟩
    have hInf : C.Infinite ↔ (p ⁻¹' ({y} : Set Nat)).Infinite :=
      hImage ▸ Set.infinite_image_iff hrInj.injOn
    change (p ⁻¹' ({y} : Set Nat)).Infinite ↔ y ∈ P
    by_cases hy : y ∈ P
    · have hHy (k : Nat) : y ∈ H k :=
        Set.mem_iInter.mp (hPinter ▸ hy) k
      have hCinf : C.Infinite :=
        (Set.infinite_range_of_injective
          ((hPairLeft y).comp Nat.succ_injective)).mono (by
            rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩
            exact ⟨(hRsucc k y).mpr (hHy k), by simp [Nat.unpair_pair]⟩)
      exact iff_of_true (hInf.mp hCinf) hy
    · have hMiss : ∃ k, y ∉ H k := by
        apply not_forall.mp
        intro hAll
        exact hy (hPinter.symm ▸ Set.mem_iInter.mpr hAll)
      obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hMiss
      have hBound : C ⊆ (fun j => Nat.pair j y) '' Set.Iic k := by
        intro z hz
        obtain ⟨hzR, hzy⟩ := hz
        have hzPair : Nat.pair z.unpair.1 y = z := by
          rw [← hzy, Nat.pair_unpair]
        refine ⟨z.unpair.1, ?_, hzPair⟩
        change z.unpair.1 ≤ k
        cases hlevel : z.unpair.1 with
        | zero => exact Nat.zero_le k
        | succ j =>
          have hjy : y ∈ H j := (hRsucc j y).mp (by
            rw [hlevel] at hzPair
            simpa only [hzPair] using hzR)
          have hjk : j < k := lt_of_not_ge (fun hkj => hk (hAnti hkj hjy))
          exact Nat.succ_le_of_lt hjk
      have hCfin : C.Finite := ((Set.finite_Iic k).image _).subset hBound
      exact iff_of_false (fun hf => hInf.mpr hf hCfin) hy
  · -- Surjectivity discharges the reviewed least-preimage supplier's
    -- termination hypothesis. Its section equation is the right inverse.
    obtain ⟨s, hs, _, hRight, _⟩ := ComputableInjectiveSection p hp hpSurj
    exact ⟨s, hs, hRight⟩

ComplementationOrderIsomorphism.proof:
by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §5, proof of Corollary 7, pp. 13–14.
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and designated defect report
  -- returned HTTP 404.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
  -- Alphabeta Math's shared item def-computable-many-one-reducibility-interface,
  -- verification step 1.1, uses a total computable Nat map with a pointwise
  -- membership iff. Negating both predicates preserves that iff and the same
  -- witness, including all singleton fibres.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-computable-many-one-reducibility-interface
  -- The article's c.e. hypothesis is retained. The isomorphism itself uses
  -- only the many-one and finite-one reductions of the representatives.
  intro A _hA finiteOneReducible finiteOneDegree F degreeOrder d dc
  have manyOneCompl {X Y : Set Nat}
      (h : ManyOneReducible (· ∈ X) (· ∈ Y)) :
      ManyOneReducible (· ∈ Xᶜ) (· ∈ Yᶜ) := by
    obtain ⟨f, hf, hmem⟩ := h
    exact ⟨f, hf, fun x => (hmem x).not⟩
  have degreeCompl {X Y : Set Nat} (h : ManyOneDegree.of X = ManyOneDegree.of Y) :
      ManyOneDegree.of Xᶜ = ManyOneDegree.of Yᶜ := by
    obtain ⟨hXY, hYX⟩ := ManyOneDegree.of_eq_of.mp h
    exact ManyOneDegree.of_eq_of.mpr ⟨manyOneCompl hXY, manyOneCompl hYX⟩
  have finiteOneCompl {X Y : Set Nat} (h : finiteOneReducible X Y) :
      finiteOneReducible Xᶜ Yᶜ := by
    obtain ⟨f, hf, hfibre, hmem⟩ := h
    exact ⟨f, hf, hfibre, fun x => (hmem x).not⟩
  have finiteOneComplIff (X Y : Set Nat) :
      finiteOneReducible Xᶜ Yᶜ ↔ finiteOneReducible X Y :=
    ⟨fun h => by simpa only [compl_compl] using finiteOneCompl h, finiteOneCompl⟩
  have classCompl (X : Set Nat) :
      Set.image compl (finiteOneDegree X) = finiteOneDegree Xᶜ := by
    rw [Set.compl_image]
    ext Y
    change (finiteOneReducible Yᶜ X ∧ finiteOneReducible X Yᶜ) ↔
      (finiteOneReducible Y Xᶜ ∧ finiteOneReducible Xᶜ Y)
    simpa only [compl_compl] using
      and_congr (finiteOneComplIff Y Xᶜ) (finiteOneComplIff Xᶜ Y)
  -- The reviewed endpoint uses set-valued classes. Taking the image of each
  -- class under complement makes the representative independence explicit.
  let map {e e' : ManyOneDegree}
      (h : ∀ X : Set Nat, ManyOneDegree.of X = e → ManyOneDegree.of Xᶜ = e')
      (D : F e) : F e' :=
    ⟨Set.image compl D.val, by
      obtain ⟨X, hX, hD⟩ := D.property
      exact ⟨Xᶜ, h X hX, (classCompl X).symm.trans (congrArg (Set.image compl) hD)⟩⟩
  let forward : F d → F dc := map (fun _ hX => degreeCompl hX)
  let backward : F dc → F d := map (fun _ hX =>
    by simpa only [compl_compl] using degreeCompl hX)
  have imageComplCompl (D : Set (Set Nat)) :
      Set.image compl (Set.image compl D) = D := by
    simp only [Set.compl_image]
    ext X
    change Xᶜᶜ ∈ D ↔ X ∈ D
    rw [compl_compl]
  -- Alphabeta Math's verification step 1.1 also gives identity and composition.
  -- The local class and relation agree definitionally with the compiled
  -- supplier. Its finiteOneRefl and finiteOneTrans check finite fibres using
  -- singletons and finite preimages of finite sets, respectively. These
  -- proofs transport the existential witnesses to any representatives.
  have le_iff {e : ManyOneDegree} {D E : F e} {X Y : Set Nat}
      (hD : D.val = finiteOneDegree X) (hE : E.val = finiteOneDegree Y) :
      @LE.le (F e) (degreeOrder e) D E ↔ finiteOneReducible X Y := by
    change (∃ U ∈ D.val, ∃ V ∈ E.val, finiteOneReducible U V) ↔ _
    rw [hD, hE]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hUV⟩
      exact ReducibilityImplications.finiteOneTrans hU.2
        (ReducibilityImplications.finiteOneTrans hUV hV.1)
    · intro hXY
      exact ⟨X, ⟨ReducibilityImplications.finiteOneRefl X,
        ReducibilityImplications.finiteOneRefl X⟩,
        Y, ⟨ReducibilityImplications.finiteOneRefl Y,
        ReducibilityImplications.finiteOneRefl Y⟩, hXY⟩
  refine ⟨{
    toFun := forward
    invFun := backward
    left_inv := fun D => Subtype.ext (imageComplCompl D.val)
    right_inv := fun D => Subtype.ext (imageComplCompl D.val)
    map_rel_iff' := ?_ }, ?_⟩
  · intro D E
    obtain ⟨X, _, hD⟩ := D.property
    obtain ⟨Y, _, hE⟩ := E.property
    have hDX : (forward D).val = finiteOneDegree Xᶜ :=
      (congrArg (Set.image compl) hD.symm).trans (classCompl X)
    have hEY : (forward E).val = finiteOneDegree Yᶜ :=
      (congrArg (Set.image compl) hE.symm).trans (classCompl Y)
    change @LE.le (F dc) (degreeOrder dc) (forward D) (forward E) ↔
      @LE.le (F d) (degreeOrder d) D E
    rw [le_iff hDX hEY, le_iff hD.symm hE.symm]
    exact finiteOneComplIff X Y
  · intro X hX
    exact classCompl X

RigidDegreeAntichain.proof:
by
  open RigidDegreeAntichainProof in
  exact ⟨structural, mass_rigid, residual_rigid,
    ae_rigid.mono (fun a ha => structural (asSet a) ha),
    residual_rigid.mono (fun a ha => structural (asSet a) ha)⟩
RigidDegreeAntichain.support:
/- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect report for
   arXiv:2609.00419 returned HTTP 404. Reference [1] is arXiv:2603.02600.
   Its Corollaries 5.4 and 5.5 give the finite-one and typicality conclusions.
   arXiv:2602.19960v3 §3 proves one-one incomparability. Finite-one
   reducibility permits more witnesses, so the structural proof follows
   §5 of reference [1]. The fixed-function measure argument follows
   arXiv:2602.19960v3, Proposition 4.1. -/
namespace RigidDegreeAntichainProof

open Set MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped ENNReal

private def Rigid (A : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Computable f → (∀ n, n ∈ A ↔ f n ∈ A) →
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → f n = n

private def FiniteOne (A B : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Computable f ∧ (∀ n, n ∈ A ↔ f n ∈ B) ∧
    ∀ y, Set.Finite {n | f n = y}

private def Antichain (A : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : ℕ → Set ℕ,
    (∀ i, ManyOneReducibilityOnNat (B i) A ∧ ManyOneReducibilityOnNat A (B i)) ∧
    Pairwise (fun i j => ¬ FiniteOne (B i) (B j) ∧ ¬ FiniteOne (B j) (B i))

private def project (i n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n.unpair.1 = 0 then n.unpair.2 else Nat.pair i n.unpair.2

private theorem computableLeft : Computable (fun n : ℕ => n.unpair.1) :=
  Computable.fst.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp

private theorem computableProject (i : ℕ) : Computable (project i) := by
  have hs : Computable (fun n : ℕ => n.unpair.2) :=
    Computable.snd.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp
  have hz : Computable (fun n : ℕ => decide (n.unpair.1 = 0)) :=
    Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp computableLeft (Computable.const 0)
  unfold project
  simpa only [Bool.cond_eq_ite, decide_eq_true_eq] using
    hz.cond hs (Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp (Computable.const i) hs)

private theorem structural (A : Set ℕ) (hA : Rigid A) : Antichain A := by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2603.02600v2, Def. 5.1 and Lemma 5.2.
  -- Alphabeta Math, lem-many-one-reducibility-is-a-preorder, steps 1.2
  -- and 2.1: compose total computable maps and check membership at each
  -- input. Here projection and the base-column section are explicit.
  -- For Sᵢ = range (Nat.pair i), the code pair 0 x stands for (x,0).
  -- The code pair (k+1) t stands for (pair i t,k+1). This explicit coding
  -- replaces enumeration of the calibrated domain and search for its inverse.
  let B (i : ℕ) : Set ℕ := {n | project i n ∈ A}
  refine ⟨B, fun i => ⟨⟨project i, computableProject i, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩,
    ⟨Nat.pair 0, Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp (Computable.const 0) Computable.id,
      fun x => by change x ∈ A ↔ project i (Nat.pair 0 x) ∈ A; simp [project]⟩⟩, ?_⟩
  have incomparable (i j : ℕ) (hij : i ≠ j) : ¬ FiniteOne (B i) (B j) := by
    rintro ⟨f, hf, hfA, hfibre⟩
    let out (x k : ℕ) := project j (f (Nat.pair (k + 1) x.unpair.2))
    have hout : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => out p.1 p.2) :=
      (computableProject j).comp (hf.comp (Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp
        (Computable.succ.comp Computable.snd)
        (Computable.snd.comp (Primrec.unpair.to_comp.comp Computable.fst))))
    -- In Theorem 5.3 the search asks for an output over Sⱼ and uses
    -- bi-immunity. Here an output projecting away from x suffices.
    -- For x ∈ Sᵢ its target fibre consists only of pair 0 x, so finite
    -- fibres of f guarantee this weaker search succeeds. The
    -- installed ComputablyEnumerableSet range lemmas serve the
    -- bi-immunity route. The singleton-fibre argument needs only
    -- the installed ManyOneReducibilityOnNat witness interface.
    have hex (x : ℕ) (hx : x.unpair.1 = i) : ∃ k, out x k ≠ x := by
      by_contra! hh
      have hcol (k : ℕ) : f (Nat.pair (k + 1) x.unpair.2) = Nat.pair 0 x := by
        let n := f (Nat.pair (k + 1) x.unpair.2)
        have heq : project j n = x := hh k
        by_cases hz : n.unpair.1 = 0
        · have hs : n.unpair.2 = x := by simpa [project, hz] using heq
          change n = Nat.pair 0 x
          rw [← Nat.pair_unpair n, hz, hs]
        · have hs : Nat.pair j n.unpair.2 = x := by simpa [project, hz] using heq
          have hj := congrArg (fun m : ℕ => m.unpair.1) hs
          simp [hx] at hj
          exact (hij hj.symm).elim
      have hinj : Function.Injective (fun k : ℕ => Nat.pair (k + 1) x.unpair.2) := by
        intro a b hab
        simpa using congrArg (fun m : ℕ => m.unpair.1) hab
      exact (Set.infinite_range_of_injective hinj)
        ((hfibre (Nat.pair 0 x)).subset (by rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩; exact hcol k))
    -- Use a guard in the witness test to make least search total off Sᵢ.
    let P (x k : ℕ) := x.unpair.1 ≠ i ∨ out x k ≠ x
    let _ : DecidableRel P := fun x k =>
      inferInstanceAs (Decidable (x.unpair.1 ≠ i ∨ out x k ≠ x))
    have hP : ComputablePred (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => P p.1 p.2) := by
      have hc : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => decide (p.1.unpair.1 = i)) :=
        Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp (computableLeft.comp Computable.fst) (Computable.const i)
      have hd : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => decide (out p.1 p.2 = p.1)) :=
        Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp hout Computable.fst
      apply Computable.computablePred
      refine (Primrec.or.to_comp.comp (Primrec.not.to_comp.comp hc)
        (Primrec.not.to_comp.comp hd)).of_eq ?_
      intro p
      simp [P]
    have htot (x : ℕ) : ∃ k, P x k := by
      by_cases hx : x.unpair.1 = i
      · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hex x hx
        exact ⟨k, Or.inr hk⟩
      · exact ⟨0, Or.inl hx⟩
    let idx (x : ℕ) := Nat.find (htot x)
    have hidx : Computable idx := Computable.find hP htot
    let g (x : ℕ) := if x.unpair.1 = i then out x (idx x) else x
    have hg : Computable g := by
      have hc : Computable (fun x : ℕ => decide (x.unpair.1 = i)) :=
        Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp computableLeft (Computable.const i)
      simpa only [g, Bool.cond_eq_ite, decide_eq_true_eq, id_eq] using
        hc.cond (hout.comp (Computable.id.pair hidx)) Computable.id
    have hgA (x : ℕ) : x ∈ A ↔ g x ∈ A := by
      by_cases hx : x.unpair.1 = i
      · have heq : project i (Nat.pair (idx x + 1) x.unpair.2) = x := by
          simp [project, ← hx]
        have hh := hfA (Nat.pair (idx x + 1) x.unpair.2)
        change project i (Nat.pair (idx x + 1) x.unpair.2) ∈ A ↔ out x (idx x) ∈ A at hh
        simpa [heq, g, hx] using hh
      · simp [g, hx]
    obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := hA g hg hgA
    let x := Nat.pair i N
    have hx : x.unpair.1 = i := by simp [x]
    have hne : out x (idx x) ≠ x := (Nat.find_spec (htot x)).resolve_left (not_not_intro hx)
    exact hne (by simpa [g, hx] using hN x (Nat.right_le_pair i N))
  exact fun i j hij => ⟨incomparable i j hij, incomparable j i hij.symm⟩

private def asSet (a : ℕ → Bool) : Set ℕ := {n | a n = true}

private noncomputable def coin : Measure Bool := Measure.uniformOfFinset Finset.univ

private local instance : IsProbabilityMeasure coin := by
  constructor
  simp [coin, Measure.uniformOfFinset_apply, ENNReal.div_self]

private noncomputable def fairCoin : Measure (ℕ → Bool) :=
  Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => coin)

private local instance : IsProbabilityMeasure fairCoin := by
  unfold fairCoin
  infer_instance

private def agrees (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (ℕ → Bool) :=
  {a | ∀ n, a n = a (f n)}

private theorem closedAgrees (f : ℕ → ℕ) : IsClosed (agrees f) := by
  change IsClosed {a : ℕ → Bool | ∀ n, a n = a (f n)}
  rw [Set.ofPred_forall]
  exact isClosed_iInter fun n => isClosed_eq (continuous_apply n) (continuous_apply (f n))

private theorem residual_agrees_compl {f : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hm : ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ f n ≠ n) :
    (agrees f)ᶜ ∈ residual (ℕ → Bool) := by
  -- Alphabeta Math, lem-cantor-and-baire-sequence-coding, steps 1.1 and
  -- 2.1: use the finite prefix basis and change an unrestricted bit.
  -- Here its new value must differ from the bit at the image coordinate.
  -- lem-open-dense-and-closed-nowhere-dense-baire-forms-are-equivalent-in-zf,
  -- steps 1.1 and 2.1: check density on each nonempty open set and apply
  -- the open-complement criterion to the closed agreement set.
  apply residual_of_dense_open (closedAgrees f).isOpen_compl
  rw [dense_iff_inter_open]
  rintro U hU ⟨a, ha⟩
  obtain ⟨_, ⟨b, N, rfl⟩, hab, hsub⟩ :=
    (PiNat.isTopologicalBasis_cylinders (fun _ => Bool)).exists_subset_of_mem_open ha hU
  obtain ⟨n, hn, hfn⟩ := hm N
  let c : ℕ → Bool := Function.update a n (!(a (f n)))
  refine ⟨c, hsub (PiNat.mem_cylinder_iff.mpr ?_), ?_⟩
  · intro k hk
    simpa [c, Function.update_of_ne (show k ≠ n by omega)] using
      PiNat.mem_cylinder_iff.mp hab k hk
  · intro hc
    have heq := hc n
    simp only [c, Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne hfn] at heq
    cases h : a (f n) <;> simp [h] at heq

private def flip (n : ℕ) (a : ℕ → Bool) (k : ℕ) : Bool :=
  if k = n then !(a k) else a k

private theorem map_flip (n : ℕ) : Measure.map (flip n) fairCoin = fairCoin := by
  have hcoin : Measure.map Bool.not coin = coin := by
    apply Measure.ext_of_singleton
    intro b
    rw [Measure.map_apply (measurable_of_finite _)
      (MeasurableSet.singleton b)]
    have hpre : Bool.not ⁻¹' {b} = {!(b)} := by
      ext a
      change (Bool.not a = b) ↔ a = Bool.not b
      cases a <;> cases b <;> decide
    rw [hpre]
    simp [coin]
  have hmeas (k : ℕ) : Measurable (fun b : Bool => if k = n then !b else b) :=
    measurable_of_finite _
  change Measure.map (fun a k => if k = n then !(a k) else a k) fairCoin = fairCoin
  unfold fairCoin
  rw [Measure.infinitePi_map_pi _ hmeas]
  congr 1
  funext k
  by_cases hk : k = n
  · simpa [hk] using hcoin
  · simp [hk]

private theorem measure_inter_agreement {C : Set (ℕ → Bool)} {n m : ℕ}
    (hC : MeasurableSet C) (hnm : n ≠ m)
    (hflip : ∀ a, flip n a ∈ C ↔ a ∈ C) :
    fairCoin (C ∩ {a | a n = a m}) = fairCoin C / 2 := by
  -- A fair-coin coordinate flip is measure preserving. It interchanges
  -- the agreeing and disagreeing halves of an event independent of n.
  let E : Set (ℕ → Bool) := {a | a n = a m}
  have hE : MeasurableSet E := measurableSet_eq_fun (measurable_pi_apply n) (measurable_pi_apply m)
  have hm : Measurable (flip n) := Measurable.of_eval fun k => by
    by_cases hk : k = n
    · simpa [flip, hk, Function.comp_def] using
        (measurable_of_finite Bool.not).comp (measurable_pi_apply n)
    · simpa [flip, hk] using (measurable_pi_apply k : Measurable (fun a : ℕ → Bool => a k))
  have hsplit : flip n ⁻¹' (C ∩ E) = C ∩ Eᶜ := by
    ext a
    change (flip n a ∈ C ∧ flip n a n = flip n a m) ↔ (a ∈ C ∧ ¬ a n = a m)
    rw [hflip]
    simp only [flip, ite_eq_right hnm.symm]
    cases a n <;> cases a m <;> simp
  have hequal : fairCoin (C ∩ E) = fairCoin (C ∩ Eᶜ) := by
    rw [← hsplit, ← Measure.map_apply hm (hC.inter hE), map_flip]
  have hdisj : Disjoint (C ∩ E) (C ∩ Eᶜ) := by
    exact disjoint_compl_right.mono Set.inter_subset_right Set.inter_subset_right
  have hunion : (C ∩ E) ∪ (C ∩ Eᶜ) = C := by
    ext a
    simp
  have hsum := measure_union (μ := fairCoin) hdisj (hC.inter hE.compl)
  rw [hunion, ← hequal] at hsum
  apply (ENNReal.eq_div_iff (by norm_num) (by simp)).2
  simpa [two_mul] using hsum.symm

private theorem measure_agrees_zero {f : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hm : ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ f n ≠ n) : fairCoin (agrees f) = 0 := by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2602.19960v3, Proposition 4.1, p. 6.
  -- We retain finite supports and halve the cylinder mass by a coordinate
  -- flip. The almost-everywhere endpoint needs only existence of the
  -- finite tests, so no effective sequence or randomness test is needed.
  have hconstraints (t : ℕ) : ∃ (s : Finset ℕ) (C : Set (ℕ → Bool)),
      MeasurableSet C ∧ agrees f ⊆ C ∧ fairCoin C = (2⁻¹ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ t ∧
      ∀ a b : ℕ → Bool, (∀ k ∈ s, a k = b k) → (a ∈ C ↔ b ∈ C) := by
    induction t with
    | zero => exact ⟨∅, univ, MeasurableSet.univ, Set.subset_univ _, by simp, by simp⟩
    | succ t ih =>
      obtain ⟨s, C, hC, hsub, hmass, hdep⟩ := ih
      obtain ⟨n, hn, hfn⟩ := hm (s.sup Nat.succ)
      have hns : n ∉ s := fun hn' => by
        have hle : n.succ ≤ s.sup Nat.succ := Finset.le_sup (f := Nat.succ) hn'
        omega
      let E : Set (ℕ → Bool) := {a | a n = a (f n)}
      have hE : MeasurableSet E :=
        measurableSet_eq_fun (measurable_pi_apply n) (measurable_pi_apply (f n))
      have hflip (a : ℕ → Bool) : flip n a ∈ C ↔ a ∈ C := by
        apply hdep
        intro k hk
        have hkn : k ≠ n := fun he => hns (he ▸ hk)
        simp [flip, hkn]
      refine ⟨insert n (insert (f n) s), C ∩ E, hC.inter hE,
        fun a ha => ⟨hsub ha, ha n⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [measure_inter_agreement hC hfn.symm hflip, hmass, pow_succ, div_eq_mul_inv]
      · intro a b hab
        have hs : ∀ k ∈ s, a k = b k := fun k hk => hab k (by simp [hk])
        have h₁ := hab n (by simp)
        have h₂ := hab (f n) (by simp)
        change (a ∈ C ∧ a n = a (f n)) ↔ (b ∈ C ∧ b n = b (f n))
        rw [hdep a b hs, h₁, h₂]
  have hle (t : ℕ) : fairCoin (agrees f) ≤ (2⁻¹ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ t := by
    obtain ⟨_, C, _, hC, hmass, _⟩ := hconstraints t
    exact (measure_mono hC).trans_eq hmass
  refine le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
  exact le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto tendsto_const_nhds
    (ENNReal.tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (by norm_num))
    (Eventually.of_forall hle)

private noncomputable def codeFunction (c : Nat.Partrec.Code) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  if h : (c.eval n).Dom then (c.eval n).get h else 0

private theorem exists_codeFunction (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : Computable f) :
    ∃ c, codeFunction c = f := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.Partrec.Code.exists_code.mp (Partrec.nat_iff.mp hf.partrec)
  refine ⟨c, funext fun n => ?_⟩
  unfold codeFunction
  rw [hc]
  simp [PFun.coe_val]

private def obeys (f : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ → Bool) : Prop :=
  a ∈ agrees f → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → f n = n

private theorem eventually_obeys {l : Filter (ℕ → Bool)}
    (f : ℕ → ℕ) (h : (∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ f n ≠ n) →
      (agrees f)ᶜ ∈ l) : ∀ᶠ a in l, obeys f a := by
  by_cases ht : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → f n = n
  · exact Eventually.of_forall fun _ _ => ht
  · have hm : ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ f n ≠ n := by push Not at ht; exact ht
    have havoids : ∀ᶠ a in l, a ∉ agrees f := h hm
    exact havoids.mono fun _ ha hfix => (ha hfix).elim

private theorem eventually_rigid {l : Filter (ℕ → Bool)} [CountableInterFilter l]
    (h : ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ f n ≠ n) → (agrees f)ᶜ ∈ l) :
    ∀ᶠ a in l, Rigid (asSet a) := by
  -- Every total computable map is represented by a partial-recursive code.
  -- The default on undefined arguments is used only to index the tests by
  -- this countable type. Each individual test applies to arbitrary maps.
  -- The countable intersection of open dense complements gives the
  -- residual conclusion, as in the same Alphabeta item, step 3.1.
  have hc : ∀ᶠ a in l, ∀ c : Nat.Partrec.Code, obeys (codeFunction c) a :=
    eventually_countable_forall.mpr (fun c => eventually_obeys _ (h _))
  refine hc.mono fun a ha f hf hself => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_codeFunction f hf
  rw [← hc]
  apply ha c
  rw [hc]
  exact fun n => Bool.eq_iff_iff.mpr (hself n)

private theorem ae_rigid : ∀ᵐ a ∂fairCoin, Rigid (asSet a) := by
  apply eventually_rigid
  intro f hf
  apply ae_iff.mpr
  have heq : {a | ¬ a ∉ agrees f} = agrees f := Set.ext (by simp)
  rw [heq]
  exact measure_agrees_zero hf

private theorem residual_rigid : ∀ᶠ a in residual (ℕ → Bool), Rigid (asSet a) :=
  eventually_rigid fun _ => residual_agrees_compl

private theorem mass_rigid : fairCoin {a | Rigid (asSet a)} = 1 := by
  have h : {a | Rigid (asSet a)} =ᵐ[fairCoin] (univ : Set (ℕ → Bool)) :=
    ae_rigid.mono fun _ ha => by simp [ha]
  rw [measure_congr h, measure_univ]

end RigidDegreeAntichainProof

PullbackReductions.proof:
by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §4, proof of Theorem 5, p. 11.
  -- The article obtains p and s from Lemma 1 (ProfileRealization). This
  -- endpoint supplies them as hypotheses. The profile and surjectivity are
  -- used in the surrounding construction. The right-inverse equation
  -- suffices for membership preservation and injectivity of the section.
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and its defect report both
  -- returned HTTP 404. The shared-library item below supplies verification
  -- step 1.1 for the computable-map membership calculation on Nat.
  intro A _P p s hp _hpSurj _hProfile hs hSection
  let C : Set Nat := Set.preimage p A
  -- Alphabeta Math, def-computable-many-one-reducibility-interface, step 1.1
  -- checks the membership equivalence for computable witnesses. Here the
  -- equation p (s y) = y gives that equivalence and the extra injectivity
  -- needed for one-one reducibility. Step 2.1 concerns string encodings.
  have hOne : OneOneReducible (fun x : Nat => x ∈ A) (fun x : Nat => x ∈ C) := by
    refine ⟨s, hs, hSection.injective, ?_⟩
    intro y
    change y ∈ A ↔ p (s y) ∈ A
    rw [hSection y]
  have hFinite := (ReducibilityImplications A C).1 hOne
  have hAC := (ReducibilityImplications A C).2 hFinite
  -- Pullback membership is definitionally membership of the image under p.
  have hCA : ManyOneReducibilityOnNat C A := by
    unfold ManyOneReducibilityOnNat
    exact ⟨p, hp, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  exact ⟨hOne, hFinite, hCA, (ManyOneDegree.of_eq_of (p := C) (q := A)).2 ⟨hCA, hAC⟩⟩

external.usage: Specialize ManyOneDegree.of_eq_of to Nat and apply its reverse implication to the reductions from C to A and from A to C.

HomogeneousRowsFromCylinderReduction.proof:
by
  intro A P p hp _ _ _ C cyl h hh _ hReduction encode decode uniformlyCE stage _ _ indexedRows hIndex V
  -- Cintioli's proof of Theorem 5, §4, p. 11, fixes p and h before
  -- forming the rows. Lemma 1 (ProfileRealization) supplies p in the caller.
  -- Here p and its profile are hypotheses. The row argument uses the
  -- computability of p and h and the reduction's membership equivalence.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=11
  -- The article passage is unnumbered. The corresponding Research Portal
  -- collection and defect report returned HTTP 404.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
  let pack (q : Nat × Nat) : Nat := Nat.pair q.1 (p (h (Nat.pair q.1 q.2)))
  let enumerate (k : Nat) : Nat := pack k.unpair
  let G : Set Nat := {z | ∃ x y, y ∈ V x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y}
  have hPair : Computable (fun q : Nat × Nat => Nat.pair q.1 q.2) :=
    Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp
  have hPack : Computable pack :=
    Primrec₂.natPair.to_comp.comp Computable.fst (hp.comp (hh.comp hPair))
  have hEnumerate : Computable enumerate :=
    hPack.comp Primrec.unpair.to_comp
  have hRange : Set.range enumerate = G := by
    ext z
    change (∃ k, enumerate k = z) ↔ ∃ x y, y ∈ V x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨k, rfl⟩
      let q := k.unpair
      exact ⟨q.1, p (h (Nat.pair q.1 q.2)), ⟨q.2, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨x, y, ⟨n, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      have hUnpair : (Nat.pair x n).unpair = (x, n) :=
        Nat.pairEquiv.symm_apply_apply (x, n)
      exact ⟨Nat.pair x n, by simp only [enumerate, pack, hUnpair]⟩

  -- Alphabeta Math's recognizability equivalence, step 1.1, searches
  -- a total enumeration for equality with the input. The reviewed supplier
  -- implements this search on Nat. Step 2.1 uses shortlex words and a
  -- time bound. The supplier's Nat bridge searches coded inputs and fuel
  -- and expresses the result with the reviewed true-bit unary encoding.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-recognizable-iff-enumerable
  have hRecognizer : REPred (fun z => z ∈ G) := by
    rw [← hRange]
    exact ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_range hEnumerate
  have hCE : uniformlyCE V :=
    (ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff true G).mp hRecognizer

  -- The assumed exhaustion of the stage enumeration applies to the whole
  -- coded graph, so the same index represents every row.
  refine ⟨hCE, hIndex V hCE, ?_⟩
  have hCylinder (x n : Nat) : Nat.pair x n ∈ cyl ↔ x ∈ A := by
    change (∃ u v : Nat, u ∈ A ∧ Nat.pair x n = Nat.pair u v) ↔ x ∈ A
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨u, v, hu, hEq⟩
      have huv : (x, n) = (u, v) := Nat.pairEquiv.injective hEq
      have hFirst : x = u := congrArg Prod.fst huv
      exact hFirst.symm ▸ hu
    · exact fun hx => ⟨x, n, hx, rfl⟩
  rintro x y ⟨n, rfl⟩
  exact (hReduction (Nat.pair x n)).symm.trans (hCylinder x n)

OracleNegativePullbackDecision.proof:
by
  open OracleNegativePullback OracleTapeSupplier.OAI.FiniteAlgebraicEnvelopes.MachineRealization in
  -- Alphabeta Math, An oracle computation has a finite query witness, steps
  -- 1.1 and 2.1. Here the run is constructed from total computability, so the
  -- finite query set is the singleton {f n}. simulate_run uses induction over
  -- the finite ordinary run, and decide_with adds its only query.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-oracle-computation-has-a-finite-query-witness
  --
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419 v1, §4, uses a halting-oracle answer to decide
  -- whether a given row ever changes after the specified stage. This lemma
  -- implements the negative branch for any total computable query map.
  -- The article omits the tape implementation. The preprocessor takes the
  -- reviewed delimiter-free input and appends the delimiter only to its
  -- output. The query evaluates the canonical numeral at the origin.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419
  --
  -- The reviewed predicate is the Shared Math Library definition. Its
  -- linked ordinary transition relation uses a clamped left move. In the
  -- simulation, a supplier stay uses a preserving right-and-left detour.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-relative-computability-and-enumerability
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-one-step-configuration-relation
  --
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta collection and defect report both
  -- returned HTTP 404. The applicable shared proof steps are cited above.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
  intro X f hf
  classical
  let g : List Letter →. List Letter := fun w => Part.some (out (f (parse w)))
  have hg : Partrec g := (comp_preprocess hf).partrec
  -- The coordinator's WordEvaluator.exists_machine candidate gives a
  -- first-blank readout. Its underlying exact-configuration lemmas give
  -- the head position and all tape cells needed by the reviewed query.
  obtain ⟨Λ, fintypeΛ, inhabitedΛ, M, start, stop, safe, eval⟩ := WordEvaluator.exists_safe_tape hg
  let : Fintype Λ := fintypeΛ
  let : Inhabited Λ := inhabitedΛ
  apply decide_with (FoldLiteral.wrapper M start)
    (some none) (fun _ => rfl) X f _ (Fintype.equivFin Work)
  intro n
  refine (StateTransition.mem_eval.mp ?_).1
  change FoldLiteral.final (out (f n)) ∈
    StateTransition.eval (OneSided.step (FoldLiteral.wrapper M start)) (FoldLiteral.initial (bits n))
  rw [FoldLiteral.wrapper_eval M start stop safe eval]
  apply Part.mem_map _
  change out (f n) ∈ Part.some (out (f (parse (bits n))))
  rw [parse_bits]
  exact Part.mem_some _

    only while the head is at a workspace cell. -/
